description-proc.hun: 1. rész: „Középiskolai Campus kialakítása” elnevezésű projekt keretében további bútorok beszerzése a Tóparti Gimnázium és Művészeti Szakgimnázium, valamint a Székesfehérvári Vasvári Pál Gimnázium részére az alábbi főbb mennyiségek vonatkozásában. A beszerzés mindösszesen 1736+7 db (Tóparti/Vasvári) bútor, egyéb kiegészítő beszerzésére vonatkozik, a bútortárgyak, egyéb kiegészítők megoszlása: - 570 db füzettartó rács, - 389 db szék, - 365 db filcbetétes padlóvédő, - 343 db asztal, melyből tanulóasztal: 281 darab, - 35 db szekrény/falipolc, - 34 db függöny A Székesfehérvári Vasvári Pál Gimnázium részére 2 db konyhabútor rendszer (mindösszesen 7 db termék) kerül beszerzésre, az alábbi megoszlásban: - 2 db konyhabútor, - 2 db mosogatótálca, - 2 db csaptelep - 1 db étkezőasztal székekkel (8 személyes, 8 db székkel). A bútorbeszerzésre vonatkozó rész további alrészre történő bontása indokolatlan, a 7 db eltérő helyszínen történő termék leszállítása külön rész keretében gazdaságtalan megvalósítást eredményezne. A részletes mennyiségek ismertetése a közbeszerzési dokumentációban. A meghatározott méretek, anyagtípusok, termék elvárások mennyiségeinél a nem szabvány termékek vonatkozásában +/- 15%-os eltérés elfogadott a releváns, meghatározott értékeknél, továbbá a színeknél is kizárólag iránymutatásként értelmezendőek a műszaki leírásban, költségvetésben rögzítettek. A fa, fém, műanyag elvárások műszaki egyenértékűsége kizárólag alapanyagon belül biztosított. A minimum 18 mm (lap)vastagságú értékkel jelölt bútoroknál a negatív irányba történő eltérés nem megengedett! A konyhabútorok és a függönyök mérete fix Ajánlatkérői előirányzat, azzal, hogy a meghatározott méretek megvalósíthatósága a szerződés teljesítése során felmérendő és szükség esetén pontosítandó! Ajánlatkérő felhívja a Tisztelt Gazdasági szereplők figyelmét, hogy a műszaki megfelelőség igazolása tekintetében Ajánlattevőnek ajánlatában fel kell tüntetnie a gyártót, a konkrét típusmegjelölést, valamint a származási helyet. Az említett elvárások igazolhatóak például "Műszaki adatlappal", amelyben szerepelnek a megajánlott termék egyértelműen beazonosítható tulajdonságai, gyártója és típusmegjelölése vagy forgalmazói/gyártói URL-lel vagy gyártói adatlappal (magyar vagy angol nyelven), feltüntetve, kiegészítve a vállalt jótállás időtartamával- esetlegesen fénykép is csatolható az adott termék előírt paramétert alátámasztó tulajdonságairól. További információ a dokumentációban. Ajánlatkérő felhívja a Tisztelt Gazdasági szereplők figyelmét, hogy a megajánlott termékekre legalább 3 év jótállást szükséges biztosítani, amennyiben a gyártói jótállás alapesetben ezt nem biztosítja, kiterjesztett vagy forgalmazó/szállító által vállalt kiegészítő jótállás vállalása az elvárás (Ptk.6:171. § (1) bekezdése szerinti vállalt jótállás). 2. rész: „Középiskolai Campus kialakítása” elnevezésű projekt keretében PVC padlóvédő burkolat a Kodolányi János Gimnázium és a Székesfehérvári Vasvári Pál Gimnázium részére az alábbi főbb mennyiségek vonatkozásában: - Kodolányi János Gimnázium: 23x45 méteres kültéri sportpálya ideiglenes védő burkolata (feltekercselhető kivitelben), évente legalább 5 alkalommal történő felhasználásra; - Székesfehérvári Vasvári Pál Gimnázium: 21x41 méteres kültéri sportpálya ideiglenes védő burkolata (feltekercselhető kivitelben), évente legalább 5 alkalommal történő felhasználásra; Mindkettő sportpálya vonatkozásában a védőburkolatnak legalább az alábbi követelményeknek kell megfelelniük: Keménység min. 80 (+ /- 5) Sh A Hőmérsékleti tartomány: -25 celsius foktól + 80 celsius fokig Vastagság: min. 3mm Sűrűség: min 1.55 g/cm3 Dupla belső megerősítéssel Színe nem lehet fekete, hogy a meglévő sportburkolatot ne színezze el- preferált a szürke színű kivitel Feltekercselhető kivitelben Alkalmasság kültéri használatra évente minimum 5 alkalommal. A padlóburkolatokra vonatkozó rész további alrészekre bontása szintén indokolatlan, a kettő darab helyszínre azonos termékek kerülnek leszállításra, a külön részek szerinti megvalósítás szintén gazdaságtalan lenne. Ajánlatkérő felhívja a Tisztelt Gazdasági szereplők figyelmét, hogy a műszaki megfelelőség igazolása tekintetében Ajánlattevőnek ajánlatában fel kell tüntetnie a gyártót, a konkrét típusmegjelölést, valamint a származási helyet. Az említett elvárások igazolhatóak például "Műszaki adatlappal", amelyben szerepelnek a megajánlott termék egyértelműen beazonosítható tulajdonságai, gyártója és típusmegjelölése vagy forgalmazói/gyártói URL-lel vagy gyártói adatlappal (magyar vagy angol nyelven), feltüntetve, kiegészítve a vállalt jótállás időtartamával- esetlegesen fénykép is csatolható az adott termék előírt paramétert alátámasztó tulajdonságairól. További információ a dokumentációban. A 321/2015. (X. 30.) Korm. rendelet 46. § (3) és (5) bekezdésében előírt „vagy azzal egyenértékű” kifejezést együtt értelmezni szíveskedjenek a felhívásban, dokumentációban esetlegesen előírt konkrét típusokkal kapcsolatban mindkettő rész vonatkozásában.

hun: Sátoraljaújhely város meglévő összes közvilágítási lámpatesteinek/fényforrásainak (2220 db) cseréjével LED világítás kerül kiépítésre. A Pataki, Kossuth Lajos, Árpád, Kazinczy utak, mint a város fő közlekedési útvonali, illetve a 37. sz. országos közút közvilágítással érintett szakaszai (M3 útbesorolási osztály) mellett az összes lámpatest lebontásra kerül, helyette a meglévő tartókon (oszlopok, kandeláberek) új LED fényforrású lámpatestek kerülnek felszerelésre. A városközponton átvezető és a várost elkerülő szakaszon 56W, a konfliktuszónáknál (gyalogos átkelőhely, kórház környéke, iskola környéke) 78W, 88W, nagyobb terület erős megvilágítása esetén 111W, 127W, 166W teljesítménnyel, amely biztosítani fogja az út besorolásának és forgalmi terheléséhez szükséges megvilágítást. A város gyűjtőútjai mellett (M4 útbesorolási osztály) az útvilágító összes lámpatest lebontásra kerül, helyette a meglévő tartókon (oszlopok, kandeláberek) új LED fényforrású lámpatest kerül felszerelésre 38W teljesítménnyel. Az új lámpatestek biztosítani fogják az utak besorolásának és forgalmi terheléséhez szükséges megvilágítást. A város közepes útjai mellett (M5 útbesorolási osztály) az összes lámpatest szintén LED fényforrású lesz. A leszerelendő lámpatestek helyére 30W teljesítményűek kerülnek felszerelésre. Az épített LED lámpatestek biztosítani fogják továbbra is a forgalmi terhelésnek megfelelő megvilágítási szintet. A város korszerűsítését érintő mellékutak (M6 osztály) a lámpatestek szintén LED fényforrásúak lesznek 20W teljesítménnyel, biztosítva ezzel, hogy a meglévő megvilágítási szint ne csökkenjen. A Kossuth Lajos téri díszkandeláberek esetén fényforráscsere szükséges, a lámpatest cseréje nélkül új, 20W kivitelű retrofit LED fényforrásokra, E27/E40 foglalattal, megrendelő által kiválasztva. A lámpatesteken elhelyezésre került HDMR OS-Zhaga M2M NB-IoT kültéri vezeték nélküli vezérlő a városi világítás optimalizálhatósága érdekében. ZHAGA csatlakozók kerültek a tervezett lámpatestekre, melyek a kültéri vezeték nélküli vezérlők előkészítéséhez szükségesek. Bővítések: Az Ipartelep utcán lámpasűrítés szükséges a megfelelő megvilágítás elérése érdekében. Rudabányácska, Károlyfalva, Széphalom településrészeken bővítések történtek. A bővítés során 42 db új lámpatestet kell elhelyezni meglévő áramszolgáltatói oszlopokon, a tervlapok és a leltár szerinti helyeken. Várható megtakarítás: A város jelenleg közvilágításának összteljesítménye 165,7 kW A teljes rekonstrukciót tartalmazó terv szerint a város felújított közvilágításának összteljesítménye 71,7 kW, ami a jelenlegi állapot 43%-ának felel meg. A részletes műszaki paramétereket a közbeszerzési dokumentáció szerinti műszaki-szakmai leírás és a költségvetés tartalmazzák. Ahol konkrét gyártmány/típus került megjelölésre, ott mindenhol „vagy azzal egyenértékű”-t kell érteni.
Sátoraljaújhely Város Önkormányzata

title-proc.eng: Darndale Park – waste removal and wall construction

eng: The Contract comprises clearance and removal of approximately 40,000 tonnes of illegally dumped waste material and construction of boundary treatments and 117m of new 2.5m high precast boundary wall and footpath between Darndale Park and a group of Traveller Accommodation site known as the Northern Sites on the north side of Dublin within the boundaries of Darndale and Priorswood. The works shall include site clearance, removal of all waste material (investigations suggest non-hazardous), removal of asbestos, removal of end-of-life vehicles and other electrical goods, treatment and removal of invasive species, construction of concrete boundary walls, construction of new footpath, environmental monitoring. There is a requirement for removal of hazardous waste should it be encountered. Temporary works shall include construction of a construction stage haul road through Darndale Park to provide site access and all associated reinstatement works, protection to all existing services, fencing of works areas etc. Design of temporary works shall form part of the works. The estimated value of the works is envisaged to be €7.5m (ex VAT) however this figure will largely be dependent on the make-up of the waste material. Applications are only sought from Contractors who have a proven track record in the works as described above. Applications are not sought from general building contractors who proposed to sub-contract the whole of the works.. Please note that this project is subject to funding. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID xxxxxxx – Input when notice created.
Dublin City Council

title-proc.eng: Met Eireann invites tenders for the monitoring of the Green House Gas-Nitrous Oxide, at its environmental monitoring site at Bray Head Valentia for a Proof Of Concept phase.

eng: Met Eireann is invites tenders for supporting the monitoring of the Green House Gas-Nitrous Oxide, at its environmental monitoring site at Bray Head Valentia Island for a Proof Of Concept phase. The tenderer must be able to deploy Instrumentation in an ICOS (Integrated Carbon Observing System) compliant fashion with respect to calibration and data analysis, for the duration of the POC. The tenderer must be able to provide specialist expertise to utilise the data from the system to provide the basis for comprehensive modelling and analysis approaches to allows for the generation of a ‘top down’ estimate of national greenhouse gas emissions of the gas. The tenderer must also provide training to local staff to ensure appropriate skills and knowledge transfer and to also produce an end of POC report.
Met Eireann

title-proc.eng: Online learning expertise and scientific advisory (UCC-VEAT-2024-02)

eng: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. This notice acknowledges that University College Cork contracted with Randbee Consultants SRL, for the provision of support and leadership of online learning resource maintenance, development and enhancement for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. Randbee Consultants SL will lead the online learning resource activities for the overall Service contract, provide technical support to implement resource solutions, contribute niche expertise to the Scientific Advisory Committee, and support Training event implementation and online content maintenance services. Randbee Consultants SRL were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They have an extensive track record of working with European and International projects, providing valuable services and training on Copernicus product applications, Earth Observation, Geographical Information Systems (GIS), statistical analysis, modelling, and web visualization tools. The company's experience with both in-person and remote training formats aligns strongly with the diverse delivery methods outlined in the overarching Service Contract. They also have experience with working for the ECMWF, and within their staff had the required expertise in satellite data, end-user applications, and teaching and learning, to contribute to the Service’s Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service – and highly beneficial professional networks. For example, their experience in successfully delivered training on Copernicus data and services in Ecuador, and in hosting online seminars, workshops, and Copernicus hackathons in various locations (e.g. Oman, Spain), demonstrated their adaptability and reach. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completed it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.
University College Cork

title-proc.eng: Online learning expertise and scientific advisory (UCC-VEAT-2024-03)

eng: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Universidad de Málaga (UMA), for the provision of support in Scientific Advisory, online learning resource enhancement, and online & in-person training for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. UMA will contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, online learning resource, and training event activities for the overall Service contract, providing niche technical, expertise and scientific oversight support. UMA were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They brought the international European Topic Centre for Spatial Analysis and Synthesis (ETC-UMA) into the Service Contract, where environmental knowledge to support evidence-based policy and decision-making at different scales is developed, supported by the work of the Khaos research group, specialised in Big Data analytics, machine learning and artificial intelligence - all of which are quickly growing topics of interest to Copernicus trainees. The ETC-UMA team have thematic skills and perspectives of high importance to the training topics the Service is expected to advise on, including environmental remote sensing, geospatial data management and publication, indicator development, ecosystems and services assessments of marine and terrestrial environments. Additionally, researchers at ETC-UMA are currently part of the core team of the European Topic Centre on Data Integration and Digitalisation (ETC/DI) supporting the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service. UMA leads on their user uptake initiatives to promote the service portfolio within the European Environment Agency, among the other ETCs and Commission Services (such as DG Agri, Eurostat, etc.), and supports stakeholder engagement at Member State level through preparing capacity building material and workshop design. As a university, UMA is a key contributor of training experience, enhanced by organising Copernicus Hackathons, their connections within the Copernicus community, and their founding role in the Copernicus Academy. As such, they bring the skills, expertise, networks, good standing and track record to meet the needs of the Service's Scientific Advisory Committee, Training Event implementation, and Online training resource development. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The institute was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.
University College Cork

description-proc.eng: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Universidad de Málaga (UMA), for the provision of support in Scientific Advisory, online learning resource enhancement, and online & in-person training for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. UMA will contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, online learning resource, and training event activities for the overall Service contract, providing niche technical, expertise and scientific oversight support. UMA were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They brought the international European Topic Centre for Spatial Analysis and Synthesis (ETC-UMA) into the Service Contract, where environmental knowledge to support evidence-based policy and decision-making at different scales is developed, supported by the work of the Khaos research group, specialised in Big Data analytics, machine learning and artificial intelligence - all of which are quickly growing topics of interest to Copernicus trainees. The ETC-UMA team have thematic skills and perspectives of high importance to the training topics the Service is expected to advise on, including environmental remote sensing, geospatial data management and publication, indicator development, ecosystems and services assessments of marine and terrestrial environments. Additionally, researchers at ETC-UMA are currently part of the core team of the European Topic Centre on Data Integration and Digitalisation (ETC/DI) supporting the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service. UMA leads on their user uptake initiatives to promote the service portfolio within the European Environment Agency, among the other ETCs and Commission Services (such as DG Agri, Eurostat, etc.), and supports stakeholder engagement at Member State level through preparing capacity building material and workshop design. As a university, UMA is a key contributor of training experience, enhanced by organising Copernicus Hackathons, their connections within the Copernicus community, and their founding role in the Copernicus Academy. As such, they bring the skills, expertise, networks, good standing and track record to meet the needs of the Service's Scientific Advisory Committee, Training Event implementation, and Online training resource development. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The institute was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

title-proc.eng: Provision of Distributed Antenna System for Haymarket

eng: The NTA is seeking tender responses from Service Providers who have proven skills, knowledge and experience to install a Distributed Antenna System (DAS) for its Haymarket office located at Haymarket House, Smithfield, Dublin 7. The DAS system installed must be able to support and facilitate signal re-broadcasting of mobile network operators throughout the building. The Service Provider will provide the following services (the “Services”). i. The design and installation of a DAS solution suitable for the NTAs mobile requirements on site in Smithfield, capable of delivery of the below minimum reception standards: o 800 MHz band o 900 MHz band (3G – Voice – will be live on the system) o 1800 MHz band (4G – Data – will be live on this system) o 2100 MHz band (3G – Voice - will be live on this system) o 2600 MHz band ii. Presenting design criteria to secure approval for technical sign-off from the MNOs and NTA prior to installation. The Service Provider will be responsible for ensuring that all services are completed in line with building fit out schedule, currently planned for Q2 2024. This is an indicative timeline. The DAS will be installed to ensure seamless mobile phone connectivity throughout the entire building. The system must be fully compliant with the latest JOTS and MIPS.
National Transport Authority_1149
Boldyn Networks Ireland Limted

title-proc.eng: In-person and online training expertise, scientific advisory (UCC-VEAT-2024-04)

eng: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork contracted with Collecte Localisation Satellites (CLS), for the provision of support of online learning resource development and enhancement, training expertise and scientific oversight for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. CLS will (i) support the online learning resource activities for the overall Service contract, providing technical support to implement resource solutions, (ii) contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, and (iii) support Training event implementation. CLS were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They have extensive experience in developing integrated offers to a broad range of Service-relevant stakeholders including: government, industry and the scientific community and services, in sectors such as Environment & climate monitoring, Mobility, Energy & infrastructures, amongst others. They have a dedicated team of data scientists who work closely with oceanographers to develop new methodologies, understandings and ocean science communications. They have coupled this with a growing, and impressive training portfolio in Earth Observation applications - critical to the Copernicus programme – and are existing suppliers of data and training materials to the Copernicus Climate Service, and Copernicus Marine Service (in addition to ESA, CNES and many other global partners, which brought considerable potential for synergies to the Service). CLS have also delivered staff training programmes to field and IT operators and end-users, while having also developed a full Moodle course for EUMETSAT, and a range of Jupyter applications and notebooks, the bedrock of the ECMWF's online training offering. Their staff are experienced in delivering in-person training on ocean scient topics such as altimetry, a key area for capacity building in the Copernicus community. In addition, they bring their oceans experience, training experience and knowledge of satellite systems to satisfy a critical niche for expertise in the Service’s Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.
University College Cork

title-proc.eng: Scientific advisory, online/in-person training, and online learning expertise (UCC-VEAT-2024-05)

eng: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Paris-Lodron Universität Salzburg (PLUS), for the provision of support in Scientific Advisory, online learning resource enhancement, and online & in-person training for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. PLUS will contribute to the online learning resource, training, and Scientific Advisory activities for the overall Service contract, providing niche technical and quality control support to implement resource solutions, contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, and support training event implementation and online content maintenance services. PLUS were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They brought their Department of Geoinformatics into the Service Team, recognized as a hub for graduate education in Geoinformatics with a distinctly international orientation. Next to its rich academic portfolio, this enables the Service to benefit from more than 30 years´ experience in distance learning and postgraduate education for upskilling professionals in geoinformatics and related subjects. PLUS have extensive experience in delivering capacity building activities within and outside Europe, employing a range of Erasmus-supported instruments. For example, the department is the initiator and coordinator of the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master "Copernicus Master in Digital Earth", and they are co-founders of the Copernicus Academy, fostering the emergence of regional and virtual Copernicus hubs. Within the Erasmus Skills Alliance project EO4GEO (2018-2022), they acted as Academic Coordinator to push the Copernicus downstream sector. Additionally, they have engaged in the downstream service evolution for 15+ years in various application areas of interest to the Copernicus community, including biodiversity monitoring, disaster response, and climate change adaptation. This, in addition to their academic portfolio, uniquely places them to contribute to the Service's Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service – while equipping the Service with their highly beneficial professional networks and Copernicus experience. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.
University College Cork

title-proc.eng: Communication & Online Learning Enhancement & Scientific Advisory (UCC-VEAT-2024-07)

eng: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Stichting Climate-KIC International Foundation (Climate-KIC), for the provision of support and leadership of online and in-person training event implementation for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. Climate-KIC will lead the event implementation activities for the overall Service contract, and contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee. Climate-KIC were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They brought their extensive networks in the worlds of business, academia, and the public and non-profit sectors into the Service team. For example, Climate-KIC are an official member of the Copernicus Academy since 2018 which has equipped them with an exceptional insight into the educational and training landscape of the Copernicus Programme - a critical requirement for this work. title-proc.eng: Communications, online learning enhancement, and scientific advisory - UCC-VEAT-2024-06

eng: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. This notice acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Evenflow SRL, for the provision of communications support, scientific advisory and technical expertise for online learning enhancement, for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. Evenflow SRL will lead the communications activities for the overall Service contract, provide technical support to promote online and in-person training, enhance the online training offering, and contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee. Evenflow SRL were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform this role in the overall Service contract. They specialise in the promotion, exploitation and market uptake of innovative technologies (primarily in the areas of Earth Observation and Satellite Navigation). Their role is centred on promotion and communications management of all information pertaining to training events and online learning content releases implemented by the Service, for which they are uniquely suited. Evenflow are already embedded in the ECMWF’s Copernicus community, providing communications support to the ECMWF in terms of their more general Copernicus communications. As such, they were uniquely placed to complement this Service, ensuring it can quickly and effectively align with the standards and procedures of Copernicus communications by the ECMWF. Evenflow are also technically and thematically equipped to play a key front-end role in enhancing the online Training offering of both the Copernicus Services, complementing the skills of the wider Service team with their niche user-facing expertise. In addition, with their track record in strategic advisory, and supporting the promotion, exploitation and market uptake of technologies noted above, they have the required expertise in satellite data uses, applications and business development to contribute their market perspectives to the Service’s Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service – in addition to bringing their highly beneficial professional networks into the Service. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.
University College Cork

title-proc.eng: Offshore Geotechnical Surveys

eng: The Contracting Entity intends to establish a Qualification System to procure the scope of services pertaining to offshore geotechnical surveys for the development of its offshore wind farm (OWF) project(s) in Ireland and the UK. The scope of services pertaining to the geotechnical surveys are intended to provide sufficient geotechnical data to allow the characterisation of the sub-seabed strata in order to refine a three-dimensional soils model of the offshore windfarm site. These details will be used to initiate the design of the WTG and sub-station foundations and to carry out a comprehensive analysis of the installation methodology. The output from the survey will directly support the subsequent Front-End Engineering & Design (FEED) activities for the OWF site. The qualification system may include projects developed by ESB, ESB Joint Venture companies (existing or yet to be formed), ESB subsidiary companies or companies ESB Group has a minority interest in. A qualification System Questionnaire setting out the requirements for qualification and information on the qualification process is available to download at : https://www.etenders.gov.ie/epps/dps/prepareViewCfTDPSWS.do?resourceId=3591629
Electricity Supply Board (ESB)

title-proc.eng: Technical assistance to the Environmental Protection Agency (Ireland) for the 5th round of noise mapping and action planning under the Environmental Noise Directive (END).

eng: The ‘Environmental Monitoring and Surveillance unit’ within the EPA Office of Radiation Protection and Environmental Monitoring (ORM) is responsible for overseeing the strategic noise mapping process required under the Environmental Noise Directive. The Environmental Noise Regulations 2018 (S.I No. 549 of 2018) , (and prior to that the Noise Regulations 2006) transpose EU Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise, more commonly known as the Environmental Noise Directive (END). This Directive aims to provide a common framework to avoid, prevent or reduce, on a prioritised basis, the harmful effects of exposure to environmental noise. It sets out a two-stage process for addressing environmental noise by requiring Member States to: • Establish the extent of the noise environment by preparing ‘strategic noise maps’ for major roads, railways, airports and agglomerations. • Based on the results of these maps, the competent authorities in each Member State is required to develop action plans to reduce the level of noise where necessary and to maintain environmental noise quality where it is good. The first 5-year noise mapping process covered the period from 2004-2008. The third (2014-18) and fourth cycles (2019-2024) addressed noise from major sources over a specified thresholds as follows: • Agglomeration with 100,000 or more inhabitants: • Major Roads which exceed 3 million vehicles per year • Major Railways with 30,000 or more train passages per year, and, • Major Airports with 50,000 or more movements per year (no change from the first cycle) The fourth cycle has now almost been completed, and preparatory work for the fifth cycle (2025-2028) will be commencing during 2025. The fifth cycle (called Round 5) will also need to incorporate the CNOSSOS-EU (common noise methodologies) as was carried out for the Round 4 cycle of mapping. • For background, the Round 4 Strategic Noise Maps are available on EPA Maps under 'Environment and Wellbeing' and 'Noise' • Some explanatory information can be viewed at: https://www.epa.ie/our-services/monitoring--assessment/noise/noise-mapping-and-action-plans/
Environmental Protection Agency

title-proc.eng: Upgrade of Met Éireann's Satellite Observation Handling System

title-proc.eng: Electrical Works to Scoil Mhuire Coolcotts Co. Wexford

title-proc.eng: 2424 - Provision of Asset Tracking License and Support

eng: This is a call to competition by AN POST for Provision of Support and Licence for Existing Asset Trackers (the “Contract”). To optimise asset management, An Post require a customer platform which should compile, store and manage data captured from these trackers in a centralised database and software system. This platform should enable real-time visibility and insights for improved asset management. The Contract, the subject of this competition is a Contract for 5 years with an option for one or more extensions by up to 3 years, at AN POST’s discretion, up to a maximum duration of 8 years subject to the terms and conditions of the Contract.

title-proc.eng: Covid 19 Vaccination System expansion

eng: In December 2020 the HSE procured a solution under Emergency Procurement Regulation 32 to support the response to the Covid 19 Immunisation programme. Salesforce licenses were procured initially for the vaccination management programme. The solution was built on Salesforce CRM platform and provided an immunisation system (Covax) and a public facing support platform (Service Cloud). Due to the extended duration of the pandemic, the changing patient care pathway and the ongoing need to support a post pandemic covid vaccination regime, continued integration and expansion to meet Public Health requirements was necessary. The solution has undergone significant development over three years, evolving from a minimum viable product into a comprehensive immunisation system capable of managing multiple vaccine types. A network of interconnected software applications, data repositories, integration points, platforms and services have been built up to create a complex and mature Immunisation Ecosystem with Covax at its core. The capability to extend Covax to meet the requirements for other immunisation programmes, such as Flu and Pneumococcal, has already been delivered and proven. Covax is now an embedded component of the national IT infrastructure used to record Covid, Influenza (Flu), and Pneumococcal vaccinations. It is currently the largest patient database in the HSE, with 4.4 million patient records and over 16 million recorded vaccinations. The HSE now intends to progress with the addition of further vaccinations leading to Covax becoming the National Immunisation Information System (NIIS). The technical sophistication and richness of the current immunisation ecosystem make it the ideal basis from which to fulfil NIIS requirements with minimal adaptation, in a timely and cost-effective manner, while avoiding duplication of existing efforts and mitigating the current clinical risks. The HSE intends to move forward as follows: - Extend the use of the Covax system to support the administration of the National Immunisation programmes - Extend the use of Service Cloud to support all HSELive communication services - Broaden the use of Salesforce CRM functionality to include other services as required This will be done through the establishment of a Dynamic Purchasing System arrangement for ongoing products and services. To ensure continuity of safe delivery of health services and a value for money return on the significant capital investment to date, the HSE will continue with the current arrangements until the new arrangement is established.
Health Service Executive (HSE)

description-proc.eng: In December 2020, the HSE procured a solution under Emergency Procurement Regulation 32 to support the response to the Covid 19 Immunisation programme. The solution was built on Salesforce CRM platform and provided an immunisation system (Covax) and a public facing support platform (Service Cloud). Due to the extended duration of the pandemic, the ongoing need for comprehensive vaccination management, and a changing patient care pathway, continued integration and expansion of the solution was required to meet Public Health requirements. Covax has undergone significant development over three years, evolving from a MVP into a comprehensive immunisation system capable of managing multiple vaccine types. Covax vaccination platform has evolved to support the following: patient account creation; vaccination recording; full patient vaccination histories; administration of multiple vaccine products; configurable interval times and doses; configurable risk factors; product-based eligibility criteria; adverse reaction capabilities; diverse vaccine administration locations. Additional functionality includes patient portal; appointment scheduling; reporting and analytics; user training platform; support platform; communication platform. With Covax embedded as the core, a network of interconnected software applications, data repositories, integration points, platforms and services have been built up to create the comprehensive and mature national immunisation ecosystem which is in use today. Vaccination records are ingested into Covax from GPs, Pharmacies, and various Community organisations. Data is enriched on Covax through integration with IHI, GP registry, Eircode, and a vaccination asset management system. National vaccination reporting is enabled though integration with the HSE’s data lake. Covax is an established and embedded cornerstone of the national IT infrastructure. It is currently the largest patient database in the HSE, with over 4.4 million patient records and over 16 million recorded vaccinations. The architecture of the Covax system is proven in terms of both performance and scale, with the recording of 400,000 vaccinations per week at peak. The Covax public-facing portal has facilitated the self-registration of 2.2 million patients for vaccination to date and appointment scheduling functionality has created over 7.5 million appointments. Since 2021, Covax has ingested over 6 million vaccination records from GPs and 2 million from pharmacies. To date, over 20,000 clinical and operational staff have been trained to use the Covax system. Embedded in the pandemic response was the requirement for HSE Live to provide public-facing support. Salesforce Service Cloud was used to provide this support, and with extensive and incremental development, this generic platform was tailored for use by multiple Covid support teams across the HSE including HSE Live, DCC team, HSE NSD (National Service Desk), Covax support and GP Resolver teams.

title-proc.eng: Upgrade of Met Éireann's Satellite Observation Handling System

eng: Met Éireann, Ireland’s National Meteorological Service, looks to upgrade its satellite observation handling system to ensure continuity of data supply, capacity for higher data rates and new data types from next-generation meteorological satellites over the next 10 years, and to increase the resilience and geo-redundancy of this data source. The supplier of the new satellite system would be required to provide and install required reception and processing hardware and software, commission and test the system and provide a service and maintenance plan.

title-proc.eng: Technical assistance to the Environmental Protection Agency (Ireland) for the 5th round of noise mapping and action planning under the Environmental Noise Directive (END).

eng: The ‘Environmental Monitoring and Surveillance unit’ within the EPA Office of Radiation Protection and Environmental Monitoring (ORM) is responsible for overseeing the strategic noise mapping process required under the Environmental Noise Directive. The Environmental Noise Regulations 2018 (S.I No. 549 of 2018) , (and prior to that the Noise Regulations 2006) transpose EU Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise, more commonly known as the Environmental Noise Directive (END). This Directive aims to provide a common framework to avoid, prevent or reduce, on a prioritised basis, the harmful effects of exposure to environmental noise. It sets out a two-stage process for addressing environmental noise by requiring Member States to: • Establish the extent of the noise environment by preparing ‘strategic noise maps’ for major roads, railways, airports and agglomerations. • Based on the results of these maps, the competent authorities in each Member State is required to develop action plans to reduce the level of noise where necessary and to maintain environmental noise quality where it is good. The first 5-year noise mapping process covered the period from 2004-2008. The third (2014-18) and fourth cycles (2019-2024) addressed noise from major sources over a specified thresholds as follows: • Agglomeration with 100,000 or more inhabitants: • Major Roads which exceed 3 million vehicles per year • Major Railways with 30,000 or more train passages per year, and, • Major Airports with 50,000 or more movements per year (no change from the first cycle) The fourth cycle has now almost been completed, and preparatory work for the fifth cycle (2025-2028) will be commencing during 2025. The fifth cycle (called Round 5) will also need to incorporate the CNOSSOS-EU (common noise methodologies) as was carried out for the Round 4 cycle of mapping. • For background, the Round 4 Strategic Noise Maps are available on EPA Maps under 'Environment and Wellbeing' and 'Noise' • Some explanatory information can be viewed at: https://www.epa.ie/our-services/monitoring--assessment/noise/noise-mapping-and-action-plans/
Environmental Protection Agency

title-proc.eng: RFT - The Supply of Forestry Field Tablet Devices

eng: Coillte invites responses to this Request for Tender (RFT) from economic operators (‘Tenderers’) for for the supply of Mobile Field Tablets, for the capture of field data and viewing information in a forest setting, both in open ground and under canopy. The device needs to be easy to view and enter data and have excellent GPS accuracy under forest canopy. It needs to be rugged and be durable enough to withstand falls and inclement weather. Coillte’s preference is that a successful vendor will supply devices that can operate Coillte’s existing and any future adapted software’s, that will include ESRI mapping products and some Bespoke software’s developed in house. Devices should be fully supported by the vendor and are robust and suitable to outdoor working environments.
Coillte CGA

title-proc.eng: 2402 - Provision of Asset Trackers, Licences and Support

eng: This is a call to competition by An Post for thr Provision of Asset Trackers, Licence and Support (the “Contract”). An Post are looking for a tracking solution that can incorporate different types of trackers using different communication technologies to track, monitor and report using a graphical user interface. To optimise asset management, An Post requires a customer platform which should compile, store and manage data captured from these trackers in a centralised database and software system. This platform should enable real-time visibility and insights for improved asset management. The Contract, the subject of this competition is a Contract for 5 years with an option for one or more extensions by up to 3 years, at An Post's discretion, up to a maximum duration of 8 years subject to the terms and conditions of the Contract.
An Post_391

The Contract, the subject of this competition is a Contract for 5 years with an option for one or more extensions by up to 3 years, at An Post's discretion, up to a maximum duration of 8 years subject to the terms and conditions of the Contract.

title-proc.eng: Habitat Mapping and Habitat Condition Assessments of the Inch Spit within Páirc Náisiunta na Mara Ciarrai

eng: In summary, the Services comprise: a new habitat mapping and habitat condition assessment surveys of Inch Spit, County Kerry, using existing and/or novel technologies as appropriate. This is to both update and improve our understanding of the occurrence and distribution of the habitats found here. Habitats at this site were last mapped in 2007-2008 during the Saltmarsh Monitoring Project and in 2004-2006 as part of the Coastal Monitoring Project – please see supporting documents for Castlemaine Harbour SAC for details of these studies: https://www.npws.ie/protected-sites/sac/000343.

title-proc.eng: Met Eireann invites tenders for the monitoring of the Green House Gas-Nitrous Oxide, at its environmental monitoring site at Bray Head Valentia for a Proof Of Concept phase.

eng: Met Eireann is invites tenders for supporting the monitoring of the Green House Gas-Nitrous Oxide, at its environmental monitoring site at Bray Head Valentia Island for a Proof Of Concept phase. The tenderer must be able to deploy Instrumentation in an ICOS (Integrated Carbon Observing System) compliant fashion with respect to calibration and data analysis, for the duration of the POC. The tenderer must be able to provide specialist expertise to utilise the data from the system to provide the basis for comprehensive modelling and analysis approaches to allows for the generation of a ‘top down’ estimate of national greenhouse gas emissions of the gas. The tenderer must also provide training to local staff to ensure appropriate skills and knowledge transfer and to also produce an end of POC report.
Met Eireann

title-proc.eng: Request for Tenders for the provision of maintenance services for Met Eireann’s meteorological and environmental monitoring instrumentation and related infrastructure.

eng: Met Éireann’s maintains a national network of automated climatological stations, which are referred to as CAMP network stations. The information from these sensors are recorded, stored and transmitted, utilising data loggers and associated communication equipment, to Met Éireann HQ, for input into the Met Éireann database. This tender relates to the provision of regular scheduled maintenance to these stations. The CAMP (Climate) network consists of 78 stations currently (this number is projected to increase to 81) located throughout the country, on a mixture of private and public land. Scheduled maintenance is completed on a 2 year rotational basis with approximately 40 sites being visited each year. All maintenance must be completed with adherence to the current WMO guidance , including, if acceptable, any amendment or update to same. Applicant should refer to https://wmo.int/about-us/governance/technical-commissions/standards-and-recommended-practices for the most recent publication. The tendering company will undertake, at a minimum, one scheduled maintenance visit to each site location every 2 year period, fulfilling the agreed requirements. The sites are grouped by region (see Site Regional Map in the Tender documentation) and the work schedule is normally planned to reflect this, However, if several issues occur at a particular station, then the scheduled maintenance for that particular site may be brought forward on occasion. Urgent, non scheduled maintenance may also be required on occasion to any of the network stations. The tenderer is invited to include, on a per station basis, a quotation for this work.
Met Eireann

title-proc.eng: Technical assistance to the Environmental Protection Agency (Ireland) for the 5th round of noise mapping and action planning under the Environmental Noise Directive (END).

eng: The ‘Environmental Monitoring and Surveillance unit’ within the EPA Office of Radiation Protection and Environmental Monitoring (ORM) is responsible for overseeing the strategic noise mapping process required under the Environmental Noise Directive. The Environmental Noise Regulations 2018 (S.I No. 549 of 2018) , (and prior to that the Noise Regulations 2006) transpose EU Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise, more commonly known as the Environmental Noise Directive (END). This Directive aims to provide a common framework to avoid, prevent or reduce, on a prioritised basis, the harmful effects of exposure to environmental noise. It sets out a two-stage process for addressing environmental noise by requiring Member States to: • Establish the extent of the noise environment by preparing ‘strategic noise maps’ for major roads, railways, airports and agglomerations. • Based on the results of these maps, the competent authorities in each Member State is required to develop action plans to reduce the level of noise where necessary and to maintain environmental noise quality where it is good. The first 5-year noise mapping process covered the period from 2004-2008. title-proc.eng: Upgrade of Met Éireann's Satellite Observation Handling System

eng: Met Éireann, Ireland’s National Meteorological Service, looks to upgrade its satellite observation handling system. It currently receives satellite meteorology data from the EUMETCast Satellite dissemination service using an antenna-based reception system at its headquarters in Dublin. Met Éireann is also in the process of establishing additional connections to the EUMETCast Terrestrial service at both its headquarters and a second data centre in Dublin, to increase resilience and redundancy in its satellite data supply. The primary aim of this procurement is to upgrade Met Éireann’s satellite observation handling system to ensure continuity of data supply, capacity for higher data rates and new data types from next-generation satellites, and to increase the resilience and geo-redundancy of this important data source. This procurement looks to achieve the following: -Obtain system layout and design guidance for an upgraded satellite reception and processing system; -Procure hardware components to facilitate the reception and processing of current and next-generation meteorological satellite observations by the satellite system. The key hardware components shall include two antenna-dish receivers, six DVB units and required cabling. Complete component requirements will be finalised based on the system design agreed upon with the Contractor; -Procure service for the replacement/installation of required hardware for new system; -Procure the required software for the handling and processing of satellite observations on the reception and processing servers, and the installation of this software; -Procure service to test and commission the new system to receive and process data from EUMETCast dissemination services; -Ensure processed data outputted by the new system is compatible with Met Éireann’s visualisation and assimilation systems; -Procure maintenance and service plan to cover the new system once operational. With an increase in satellite data rates expected within 2024, the capacity of the supplier to perform the replacement of the system within a short time frame will be an important element.
Met Eireann
CGI Deutschland B.V. AND Co. KG

title-proc.eng: Mobile Data Collection Platform.

eng: The current contract with AMT Sybex is set to expire on January 22, 2025. At tender stage in 2017 it was considered that a seven-year term would be sufficient as it was anticipated that the mobile data collection functionality would be incorporated into other enterprise-wide systems during the term of the contract, negating the need for a separate standalone platform. However, while it is still intended to incorporate this functionality into a separate enterprise solution (e.g. as part of the proposed SAP upgrade), since this system is core to the IÉ Asset Management System and is also utilised by IÉ Safety Teams across the organisation, continuity of service is required. The integration of Fieldreach into IÉ's operations has been extensive, with the platform being deeply embedded in engineering workflows and asset management activities. Transitioning to a new provider at this stage would introduce significant technical and economic challenges: • Technical Complexity and Integration Costs: The integration of Fieldreach with IÉ’s SAP ECC system and other critical business processes was a highly customized and iterative process. A new provider would necessitate substantial redevelopment and re-integration, leading to high costs and potential disruptions in service. If a new system was to be procured, an alternative integration layer between SAP and the new tool would have to be designed, built and tested. This would require resources from GITT, IÉ technical staff and a third party integration partner. It is anticipated that the costs associated with these works would be in the region of €1M (excl. VAT). Further additional duplication of costs and risk would be incurred by transferring data from the current suppliers’ servers to those of a new supplier. • Operational Disruption: Adopting a new platform would require extensive retraining of approximately 800 users. This transition period could significantly impact productivity and the efficiency of our maintenance and asset management activities, risking compliance and operational integrity. 3. SUMMARY On the basis of the above and based on the substantial technical and economic implications, IÉ is seeking approval to conclude negotiations with AMT Sybex with a view to extending the term of this contract for a further period of up to 5 years up to January 2030, during which, it is anticipated the platform will be phased out as IÉ transitions to another enterprise solution. By extending the contract with AMT Sybex, IÉ can ensure the continuity of critical asset management operations, avoid unnecessary disruptions, and maintain operational efficiency. The continuation of the current platform will facilitate a seamless workflow for our staff and uphold the standards of our asset management processes.
Iarnród Eireann-Irish Rail

title-proc.eng: New Primary School for Adamstown Castle Educate Together - Electrical Specialist

eng: Expressions of Interest (EOI) are invited from suitably qualified Electrical Specialists for the construction of a new primary school for Adamstown Castle Educate Together, Adamstown, Co. Dublin. The project involves the development of a new 32-classroom primary school, including a 4-classroom Special Educational Needs (SEN) base, two combined General Purpose (GP) rooms, ancillary accommodation, and all associated site development works, including car parking and new sports pitches. title-proc.eng: 2424 - Provision of Asset Tracking License and Support

eng: This is a call to competition by AN POST for Provision of Support and Licence for Existing Asset Trackers (the “Contract”). To optimise asset management, An Post require a customer platform which should compile, store and manage data captured from these trackers in a centralised database and software system. This platform should enable real-time visibility and insights for improved asset management. The Contract, the subject of this competition is a Contract for 5 years with an option for one or more extensions by up to 3 years, at AN POST’s discretion, up to a maximum duration of 8 years subject to the terms and conditions of the Contract.

title-proc.eng: Request for Tenders for the provision of maintenance services for Met Eireann’s meteorological and environmental monitoring instrumentation and related infrastructure.

eng: Met Éireann’s maintains a national network of automated climatological stations, which are referred to as CAMP network stations. The information from these sensors are recorded, stored and transmitted, utilising data loggers and associated communication equipment, to Met Éireann HQ, for input into the Met Éireann database. This tender relates to the provision of regular scheduled maintenance to these stations. The CAMP (Climate) network consists of 78 stations currently (this number is projected to increase to 81) located throughout the country, on a mixture of private and public land. Scheduled maintenance is completed on a 2 year rotational basis with approximately 40 sites being visited each year. All maintenance must be completed with adherence to the current WMO guidance , including, if acceptable, any amendment or update to same. Applicant should refer to https://wmo.int/about-us/governance/technical-commissions/standards-and-recommended-practices for the most recent publication. The tendering company will undertake, at a minimum, one scheduled maintenance visit to each site location every 2 year period, fulfilling the agreed requirements. The sites are grouped by region (see Site Regional Map in the Tender documentation) and the work schedule is normally planned to reflect this, However, if several issues occur at a particular station, then the scheduled maintenance for that particular site may be brought forward on occasion. Urgent, non scheduled maintenance may also be required on occasion to any of the network stations. The tenderer is invited to include, on a per station basis, a quotation for this work.
Met Eireann
NVM Limited

title-proc.eng: Farm Plan Grassland Monitoring 2025-2027

eng: The National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS) require a contractor/contract team to carry out baseline and review surveys of Annex-quality grasslands and good quality semi-natural grasslands on a subset of NPWS Farm Plan sites. It is envisaged that c.20-25 farms will be included. Close liaison with the NPWS Grassland Ecologists and with the NPWS Agri-Ecology Unit will be required throughout. This work will need to be done by an experienced botanist(s), and fieldwork should take place between May and late August. Final deliverables will be due by early October 2027, with interim deliverables due in October of each year.
Department of Housing Local Government and Heritage

title-proc.eng: Supplier To Provide FOX615 Multiplexer Equipment, Services and Technical and Resource support pursuant to a framework agreement. TR581

eng: General Description of the Proposed Contract The Contracting Entity intends to procure material supplies for the provision of FOX615 equipment to expand ESB’s existing FOX615 network as well as a standalone project for the replacement of FOX515 with FOX615 multiplexers. It is also intended to procure support services for the FOX515 replacement program consisting of design, project management and commissioning resources. It is proposed that the Contract will include the following (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): • Provision of FOX615,FOX612 equipment to include full suite of modules available for ongoing projects. • Provision of FOX615,FOX612 equipment to include full suite of modules available for 515 replacement project. • Associated licenses for all equipment/cards. • Annual SLA for all FOX615FOX612 equipment • Project Management resource for FOX515 upgrade project • Technical design resource for FOX515 upgrade project • Technical support for future FOX615,612 related projects • Field based installation commissioning resources for FOX515 upgrade project. • Training on FOX615/612 equipment and associated platforms • Ongoing Foxman NMS upgrades and support It is a requirement that the successful service provider will have experience in delivering a solution of similar type and scale to that being sought by ESB.
Electricity Supply Board ( ESB )
Hitachi Energy Ireland

title-proc.eng: 9231 Nationwide Tree Analysis using Lidar and Imagery

eng: IE has a requirement for aerial drone surveys and tree analysis around our critical infrastructure assets, to include: • Visual Safety Inspections • Tree and Vegetation analyses • Fenceline analyses • Worksite Photography • Topographical Surveys/Structures Inspection • Thermal Imaging Surveys IE are seeking companies; with core expertise in imagery collection and remote sensing and who can produce on demand imaging and data that is highly accurate and comprehensive. • who can provide an end-to-end service, from data capture, processing and analysis to final reporting back to the client • with the resources in place to collate and analyse remotely sensed data recorded, proficient in the use of GIS tools and experienced with mapping, surveying, 3D modelling and tree identification and analyses • who must be a registered and in date UAS operator with IAA and have trained pilots with relevant certs of competency.
Iarnród Eireann-Irish Rail

title-proc.eng: Bus Éireann Vehicle Spare Parts Qualification Panel

eng: Bus Éireann proposes establishing a Vehicle Spare Parts Qualification panels of potential suppliers which will be maintained for a period of eight (8) years from the date of establishment, unless terminated earlier by the Contracting Authority. The Qualification Panels will be established in respect to different parts categories as set out below. Applicants may apply for one or more Panels. Panel 1 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance for Body Parts Panel 2 - Supply of Parts, Repair and Maintenance of Chassis Panel 3 - Supply of Parts, Repair and Maintenance of Body Panels and Structure Panel 4 - Supply of Parts, Repair and Maintenance of Glazing Panel 5 - Supply of Parts, Repair and Maintenance of Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning Systems Panel 6 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Hoses and Pipes Panel 7 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Exterior and Interior Fittings Panel 8 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Ancillary Onboard Equipment Panel 9 - Supply of Tyres and Wheels Panel 10 - Supply of Parts to, Repairs and Maintenance of Braking Systems Panel 11 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Suspension and Steering Systems Panel 12 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance for General Driveline Systems Panel 13 – Supply of Filters Panel 14 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Electrical and Electronic Components Panel 15 - Supply of Miscellaneous Electric or Electronic Components Panel 16 - Supply of Miscellaneous Mechanical or Electronic Components Successful applicants will form part of the Qualification Panel. Being on the Qualification Panel does not give the supplier any guarantee of work but may enable the supplier to tender for framework agreements, and contracts for individual projects, to be set up through the Qualification Panel from time to time. When a competition for a particular framework agreement or contract from the Qualification Panel is required, registered applicants may be taken through a further pre-qualification process to determine those to be invited to tender or negotiate. Turnover will be used to determine which Panel member(s) will be invited to tender based on the overall value of the framework agreement or contract. When determining which companies will be invited to tender, only those with a turnover of twice the annual value of the contract will be invited. Applicants who have been deemed suitably qualified may be invited to submit a formal tender for the requirements that arise during the Qualification Panel term. This Notice does not prevent the Contracting Authority from issuing other contract notices for specific requirements from time to time, including procurements outside the Qualification Panel for requirements falling within the scope of the Qualification Panel.
Bus Eireann/Irish Bus

title-proc.eng: Award of Contract to Breffni Group Ltd. for Waste Removal and Wall Construction in Darndale Park

eng: Dublin City Council has awarded a contract to Breffni Group Ltd. The Contract comprises clearance and removal of approximately 40,000 tonnes of illegally dumped waste material and construction of boundary treatments and 117m of new 2.5m high precast boundary wall and footpath between Darndale Park and a group of Traveller Accommodation site known as the Northern Sites on the north side of Dublin within the boundaries of Darndale and Priorswood. The works shall include site clearance, removal of all waste material (investigations suggest non-hazardous), removal of asbestos, removal of end-of-life vehicles and other electrical goods, treatment and removal of invasive species, construction of concrete boundary walls, construction of new footpath, environmental monitoring. There is a requirement for removal of hazardous waste should it be encountered. Temporary works shall include construction of a construction stage haul road through Darndale Park to provide site access and all associated reinstatement works, protection to all existing services, fencing of works areas etc. Design of temporary works shall form part of the works.
Dublin City Council
Breffni Group Ltd.

title-proc.eng: AG3141C - RFT for Land Surveying Equipment and Soils and Concrete Laboratory Equipment comprising of two (2) Lots for Technological University of the Shannon Midwest

eng: LOT 1: LAND SURVEYING EQUIPMENT This procurement package is for 6 number survey grade, lightweight and compact Real Time Kinematic (RTK) Global Positioning Systems (GPS) Receiver units for various satellite positioning tasks in Land Surveying, Civil Engineering and Construction applications and each unit to consist of a dual frequency GNSS Receiver, Controller, with Surveying and Setting out Software, Pole, Brackets, Chargers and an Educational Network License valid for a five-year period. The Receiver and Pole must be lightweight, compact and be able to operate efficiently in challenging canopy environments. The pole mounted controller must be tough, durable, weather resistant and the operating software plus must meet the minimum specifications. LOT 2: SOILS EFFECTIVE STRESS TRIAXIAL TEST AND CONCRETE COMPRESSION MACHINE This procurement package consists of Soils – Effective Stress Triaxial A soils triaxial testing kit with data acquisition for 100 mm diameter samples and add on components including load measurement, strain measurement, pore pressure measurement, volume change measurement, de aired water system, pressure system, data acquisition and analysis software, triaxial cell and accessories. and Concrete - Compression Machine An automatic compression machine 2000 kN capacity for concrete blocks and cylinders up to 160 x 320 mm and concrete cubes up to 200 mm to conform to EN 12390-4 and EN 772-1 with ancillary hardware and software components

title-proc.eng: 9168 Design and Build Capacity Enhancement Works at Connolly Station

eng: This is a call to competition by IE for the procurement of a Design and Build Contractor to deliver capacity enhancement works at Connolly Station, part of the DART+ Programme. DART+ is a transformative programme of projects that aims to modernise and improve existing rail services in the Greater Dublin Area (GDA). The DART network will increase from 50 kilometres to 150 kilometres transforming commuter train travel in the Greater Dublin Area. It will provide a sustainable, electrified, reliable and more frequent rail service improving capacity in all rail corridors serving Dublin, bringing DART travel with all its benefits to new and existing communities. The provision of a new electrified fleet will improve capacity and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The successful Contractor shall develop the detailed design of the proposed alterations to Connolly Station. The Contractor shall subsequently construct the works, test and commission all systems they install and provide as-built documentation and drawings accurately detailing the works as constructed. Works will need to integrate into the existing operational station, with extensions to systems including (but not limited to) low voltage power, lighting, HVAC, CCTV, Customer Information Systems, Public Address, fire detection and suppression systems and help points.

description-proc.eng: This is a call to competition by IE for the procurement of a Design and Build Contractor to deliver capacity enhancement works at Connolly Station, part of the DART+ Programme. DART+ is a transformative programme of projects that aims to modernise and improve existing rail services in the Greater Dublin Area (GDA). The DART network will increase from 50 kilometres to 150 kilometres transforming commuter train travel in the Greater Dublin Area. It will provide a sustainable, electrified, reliable and more frequent rail service improving capacity in all rail corridors serving Dublin, bringing DART travel with all its benefits to new and existing communities. The provision of a new electrified fleet will improve capacity and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The successful Contractor shall develop the detailed design of the proposed alterations to Connolly Station. The Contractor shall subsequently construct the works, test and commission all systems they install and provide as-built documentation and drawings accurately detailing the works as constructed. Works will need to integrate into the existing operational station, with extensions to systems including (but not limited to) low voltage power, lighting, HVAC, CCTV, Customer Information Systems, Public Address, fire detection and suppression systems and help points.

description-proc.eng: MetroLink will provide a high speed, high capacity, high frequency, modern and efficient public transport service for passengers travelling along the Swords/Airport to City Centre corridor in Dublin, which will be capable of integration with other modes of public transport. Further information on MetroLink is available at www.metrolink.ie/ In advance of the MetroLink main infrastructure works contracts, TII will commence the procurement of the Enabling Works Programme. The Enabling Works Programme comprises the establishment of a suite of framework agreements and qualification systems select contractors to deliver enabling works which will commence in advance of the main infrastructure works contracts (in respect of civil engineering, tunnelling and station works). The enabling works will include the removal and/or relocation of existing utilities, archaeology, heritage items (for storage/replacement) and buildings from site and undertaking other survey activities. To deliver the enabling and advance works for MetroLink, TII intends to establish 3 no. multi-party framework agreements as listed below each through a negotiated procedure with a prior call for competition. • Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework; • Utilities Framework; and • Civils Enabling Works Framework. TII also intends to establish a qualification system for independent environmental monitoring and a qualification system for archaeology services as part of the Enabling Works Programme. The proposed duration of the framework agreements is 8 years with an option to extend for 4 years to facilitate the procurement of any associated works that may be required over the duration of the Frameworks. This PIN is in connection with the Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework. The purpose of this PIN is to alert the market to TII’s intention to undertake market consultation and subsequently commence a procurement in Q3 2025. It is anticipated that the prequalification documentation will be issued in Q3 2025 with the instructions to tenderers issued in Q4 2025 or Q1 2026. TII intends to utilise the NEC4 Engineering Construction Contract (ECC) form of contracts for call offs placed under this framework. Interested parties can register their interest at https://www.etenders.gov.ie Any interested parties wishing to respond to the market consultation in advance of procurement commencement, are required to send a request to the following email address supplychainmetrolink@tii.ie by 12:00hrs on the 23rd May 2025 seeking to be issued with a copy of the briefing pack for review and completion of the questionnaire contained within the pack. The questionnaire is required to be completed in full and returned by the closing date of the 27th May 2025 by 12:00hrs to the following email address supplychainmetrolink@tii.ie. Following receipt of completed questionnaires from interested parties, TII proposes to invite selected participants to provide further information by way of one-to-one clarification meetings to be held on the 3rd , 4th and 5th June 2025. To be deemed an interested party you must register your interest on supplychainmetrolink@tii.ie. TII intends to hold a webinar for the registered interested parties in relation to this procurement on May 29th 2025 at 12:00hrs. TII previously issued a PIN in connection with the MetroLink Advance Works packages for market consultation (reference OJ S 217/2023 10/11/2023)

title-proc.eng: LA3319C - MTU - CFT - Open Procedure for the Supply, Delivery, Installation and Commissioning of Analytical Systems [2 Lots]

eng: MTU - Munster Technological University request the supply, delivery, installation and commissioning of two (2) lots: Lot 1 - Energy Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence System (EDXRF Analyser) One (1) x EDXRF Analyser to deliver routine elemental measurements across a diverse range of matrices from low viscosity liquids to solids, metals, slurries, powders, pastes and thin films. Must be flexible and easy to use and appropriate for research, industrial and environmental monitoring applications. Must be suitable for both technical and non-technical operators. The instrument should be capable of conducting, with high precision and accuracy, quantitative, qualitative and semi-quantitative (standardless) analysis from sub-ppm level to one hundred percentage. Lot 2 - Biodegradation Test System One (1) x Biodegradation Test System for analysing the degradation of plastics, composting process, microbial activity studies, soil respiration rate, soil health, microbial respiration, etc along with the ability to control environmental conditions and measure gases to calculate biodegradation rates. Must be compliant with international norms such as ISO 14855 with options for different volume sample vessels and numbers.
