The proposed services shall involve but not be limited to: - Provision of strategic/ expert advisory services in any of the listed areas - Professional services secondments - Provision of all deliverables as required in the relevant Phases of the Iarnród Éireann Project Management Procedures - Provision of advice on planning and other statutory processes - Development of realistic alternative options for the implementation of a project or business objectives. These alternatives may involve different routes or alignments, alternative designs, or substitute approaches that could also deliver the core project objectives

description-proc.eng: Iarnród Éireann (IÉ) is seeking expressions of interest from suitably qualified applicants to participate in the pre-qualification process to establish a Qualification System (QS) for Professional Services. This qualification system is to facilitate the delivery of professional services that integrate expertise from multiple fields to provide comprehensive solutions for IÉ current and future projects, as well as its business plan objectives. The proposed services shall involve but not be limited to: - Provision of strategic/ expert advisory services in any of the listed areas - Professional services secondments - Provision of all deliverables as required in the relevant Phases of the Iarnród Éireann Project Management Procedures - Provision of advice on planning and other statutory processes - Development of realistic alternative options for the implementation of a project or business objectives. These alternatives may involve different routes or alignments, alternative designs, or substitute approaches that could also deliver the core project objectives

title-proc.eng: Panel for Provision of mentoring and related services for the Local Enterprise Office in Leitrim County Council

eng: The purpose of this Contract Notice is to establish a Panel of Mentors for a range of Lots as noted at section 2.2 of the RFT for the Local Enterprise Office in Leitrim County Council. LEO Leitrim is compiling a panel of mentors, from which future mentor assignments for a 3-year period will be selected. Applications are invited from mentors with appropriate skills and experience that wish to be included in the LEO Leitrim mentor panel. Applications will be accepted throughout the lifecycle of the Panel at any stage, however in order to be considered for the first tranche of contracts, applicants should apply by 1st June 2026. The existing Panel will expire on the 31st July 2026, and will be replaced by this Panel which will operate from 1st August 2026 for a period of 3 years.

title-proc.eng: Establishment of Five Panels for the provision of Emergency Accommodation for The DRHE

eng: Dublin City Council invites applications for the establishment of 5 panels for the provision of Emergency Accommodation Services at centres within the Dublin Regional Homeless Executive (DRHE). A total of 5 Panels will be established for the following 5 areas: Lot 1 – Dublin North Lot 2 – Dublin South Lot 3 – Fingal Lot 4 – South Dublin Lot 5 – Dún-Laoghaire Rathdown The panels will be established for a maximum period of two (2) years. The panels will be continually open for access. Should the panel cease to operate, all members will be notified via www.etenders.gov.ie. This will not affect the delivery of any contracts awarded under the panels. The estimated additional Emergency Accommodation requirements for the DRHE for 2024 is estimated to be in the region of 2,000 beds per annum, subject to prevailing circumstances. It is emphasised, however, that these figures are provided strictly for indicative purposes only as there is no guaranteed expenditure under the Panels. Should the value of the Panel be expended, and/or the duration of the Panel extended, a PIN notice will be published in both instances on eTenders/OJEU clearly indicating the extension and revised value for any extension to the Panel system. Please note that this project is subject to funding. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 3578695– Input when notice created.

description-proc.eng: Dublin City Council invites applications for the establishment of 5 panels for the provision of Emergency Accommodation Services at centres within the Dublin Regional Homeless Executive (DRHE). A total of 5 Panels will be established for the following 5 areas: Lot 1 – Dublin North Lot 2 – Dublin South Lot 3 – Fingal Lot 4 – South Dublin Lot 5 – Dún-Laoghaire Rathdown The panels will be established for a maximum period of two (2) years. The panels will be continually open for access. Should the panel cease to operate, all members will be notified via www.etenders.gov.ie. This will not affect the delivery of any contracts awarded under the panels. The estimated additional Emergency Accommodation requirements for the DRHE for 2024 is estimated to be in the region of 2,000 beds per annum, subject to prevailing circumstances. It is emphasised, however, that these figures are provided strictly for indicative purposes only as there is no guaranteed expenditure under the Panels. Should the value of the Panel be expended, and/or the duration of the Panel extended, a PIN notice will be published in both instances on eTenders/OJEU clearly indicating the extension and revised value for any extension to the Panel system. Please note that this project is subject to funding. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 3578695– Input when notice created.

title-proc.eng: AFBI03-ITT03 Working at Height Expertise and Supervision

eng: The British Trust for Ornithology (BTO) and The Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) are project partners in the ACCLIMATISE project, supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB). ACCLIMATISE is led by the Agri-Food and Biosciences Institute (AFBI). Within this project, BTO is leading Work Package 2: ‘Transboundary Conservation Strategies and Sustainable Management of Marine Predators’. RSPB and BTO are co-leading the ornithological work within the project; this specifically includes seabird tracking and diet analysis, at sea surveys, passive acoustic monitoring, and developing a transboundary seabird conservation strategy and action plans for priority threatened seabird species. BTO and RSPB are looking for suitably qualified and experienced companies to Tender for the provision of Working at Height (WAH) expertise as part of the ACCLIMATISE project between May and August 2026. BTO and RSPB staff are trained as Industrial Rope Access Techniques Association (IRATA) Level 1 Operatives and for each Lot in this Call for Tender (CfT) are seeking field supervision from IRATA certified technicians (Level 3 and Level 2). The work will be focused on facilitating access and supervising researchers at seabird colonies across Northern Ireland. Specifications for the work are split into two Lots, Lot 1, led by BTO and Lot 2, led by RSPB. In both cases, the work carried out by the Supplier will be the same, namely enabling the safe access of Level 1 trained BTO and RSPB staff to seabird colonies in coastal locations in Northern Ireland in order to catch birds for GPS tagging as part of the ACCLIMATISE project. The primary difference between the Lots is the location of work. In both cases, the first two weeks of catching work will be located on Rathlin Island (55.29238, -6.19234), where BTO and RSPB will be working as a single unit. However, for the final two weeks BTO and RSPB teams will be split, with RSPB continuing to work on Rathlin, and BTO moving on to colonies located in Portrush (55.19821, -6.67199) and Newcastle (54.18917, -5.87803). This will result in the contractor supplying IRATA Level 3 and Level 2 support on Rathlin to a single team at the start of the field season but once BTO leave the island, concurrent Level 3 and Level 2 support will also be necessary on the mainland.

title-proc.eng: LA3319C - MTU - CFT - Open Procedure for the Supply, Delivery, Installation and Commissioning of Analytical Systems [2 Lots]

eng: MTU - Munster Technological University request the supply, delivery, installation and commissioning of two (2) lots: Lot 1 - Energy Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence System (EDXRF Analyser) One (1) x EDXRF Analyser to deliver routine elemental measurements across a diverse range of matrices from low viscosity liquids to solids, metals, slurries, powders, pastes and thin films. Must be flexible and easy to use and appropriate for research, industrial and environmental monitoring applications. Must be suitable for both technical and non-technical operators. The instrument should be capable of conducting, with high precision and accuracy, quantitative, qualitative and semi-quantitative (standardless) analysis from sub-ppm level to one hundred percentage. Lot 2 - Biodegradation Test System One (1) x Biodegradation Test System for analysing the degradation of plastics, composting process, microbial activity studies, soil respiration rate, soil health, microbial respiration, etc along with the ability to control environmental conditions and measure gases to calculate biodegradation rates. Must be compliant with international norms such as ISO 14855 with options for different volume sample vessels and numbers.

title-proc.eng: Tender for Project Shine for the Design, Supply and Install of Fire Suppression and Fire Abatement system at MEDITE Europe DAC ‘26

eng: MEDITE Europe DAC is investing in new plant and equipment under the title Project Shine. Project Shine involves the installation of the following: • Wet fuel handling systems. • Dry Fuel handling systems. • 56MW Biomass Energy Plant. • MDF Core + face dryers. • Services + utilities to the above, mainly: o Electrical distribution MCC’s o Compressed air o Water treatment systems o Fire detection + suppression o Natural Gas o Steam Project Shine has commenced the construction phase of Project Shine and proposals are sought for the supply of Fire Protection and Suppression to the various plant, equipment and buildings. The scope involves designing the fire protection systems to deliver the required volumes and density in order to comply with relevant standards. Medite DAC complies with NFPA standards and all equipment/pipework/valves/fittings etc are all FM approved. Existing Setup MEDITE’S existing fire mains schematic can be seen in Appendix 3. The system is designed to and complies with NFPA standards. The system comprises of: • 1 no. 1,500 GPM/125 PSI Mather + Pratt electric pump. • 1 no. 1,500 GPM/125 PSI Mather + Pratt diesel pump. • 200mm diameter ring main. • Various PIV, AV’s and fire hydrants. • The system is configured as a dry system. Scope of work The Scope of Work is to design, supply + install fire suppression/protection to the following areas: 1) Wet Fuel Equipment (estimated availability date Jun’27): o Wet Fuel from yard system o On-site Chipping System o Chipped Truck Delivery System o 51.270 Reject conveyor head + tail deluge (push button from control room) o 51.310 Tube conveyor feeding existing line #2 energy plant head + tail deluge (push button from control room) o 51.250 Tube conveyor feeding energy plant walking floor head + tail deluge (push button from control room) 2) Dry Fuel System (estimated availability date Jun’27): o 1 no. Edge Trim Silo: o 1 no. Dust Silo o Supply to each spark extinguisher spray nozzle (where runs are external the need to be complete with trace heating, lagging + cladding). 3) Energy Plant (EP) – Supplier (estimated availability date Jun’27) o Energy Plant Wet Fuel System o Energy Plant Dry Fuel System o Energy Plant Furnace o Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP) o Thermal Oil System 4) Dryer – Supplier (estimated availability date Nov’27) o Core Dryer o Facer Dryer 5) Ancillary Plant + Buildings (estimated availability date Feb’27) o Energy Plant MCC sprinkler o Energy Plant Therma Oil Primary Pump Room sprinkler o Energy Plant MCC AV room o Dryer MCC sprinkler o Wet Fuel MCC sprinkler o Wet Fuel AV room o Energy Plant AV room o 2 No. transformers at EP MCC mist system o 3 No. transformers at Dryer MCC mist system o Various Switchgear o 2 no. emergency generators mist system o Condensate return ** Drawings that will be essential to pricing this tender will be made available once the attached Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) has been signed and returned to us. Please see Appendix 3 for the full list of Additional Drawings.** *** Please see attached Tender Document for the full and completed scope of works ***
Medite Europe DAC

title-proc.eng: Exhibition Design, Manufacture and Fit-Out Services for Donegal Famine Heritage Centre CLG (trading as The Workhouse), Dunfanaghy, Co. Donegal

eng: The Donegal Famine Heritage Centre CLG (trading as 'The Workhouse') seeks to appoint a suitably qualified service provider to deliver the final design, production, and fit-out of a modern museum exhibition at The Workhouse, Dunfanaghy, Co. Donegal. Project Context and Funding The Workhouse, Dunfanaghy has been awarded grant funding by Failte Ireland through the Coast-to-Coast Capital Investment Scheme. This project is a cornerstone of the organisation's strategy, which aims to quintuple visitor numbers and revenue by transforming the site into a premier, year round, all weather destination on the Wild Atlantic Way. Core Deliverables: The Service Provider will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of the exhibition, including: Final Interpretive and Spatial Design: Utilising the provided Draft Interpretive Plan and Content Framework to develop a high-quality, universally accessible visitor journey across an envisaged five distinct zones. This includes proposing a creative repositioned layout for internal partition walls to optimise visitor flow, maximising physical wall space, and the design, off-site fabrication, and installation of a detailed, historically accurate physical scale model of the original Workhouse building and grounds to serve as a central interpretive anchor. Content and Language Management: Collaborating closely with the Workhouse Working Group to edit and finalise all exhibition scripts. Deliverables include fully bilingual (English and Irish/Gaeilge) printed and digital displays to ensure strict compliance with the Official Languages (Amendment) Act 2021, alongside a professionally recorded four-language self-guided audio tour delivered via both proprietary devices and web-hosted smartphone frameworks. Technological Integration: Procuring, programming, installing, and commissioning all multimedia and audio-visual (AV) elements. This includes immersive digital media treatments and a dedicated, high-capacity Digital Archive Explorer interactive kiosk. Physical Fit-Out, Enabling Works and Heating Upgrades: Managing the complete site preparation, including the safe demolition and lawful disposal off-site of legacy exhibition fixtures. Physical works include constructing agreed internal partition walls, executing all necessary first/second-fix electrical, and decorative trades, and installing a centralised ambient climate monitoring display (in reception area). The Service Provider must also supply and commission an active, humidity control solution (with a total prohibition on external stone wall penetrations) and supply and commission a modern, energy-efficient heating upgrade compliant with Regulation (EU) 2024/1103 for the exhibition space. Please note that all works, installations, and commissioning under this contract must be fully completed, validated, and handed over to the Contracting Authority by no later than 30th March 2027.
Donegal Famine Heritage CLG trading as ''The Workhouse Dunfanghy''

title-proc.eng: Limerick City and County Council Oak Lodge Hostel Fire Safety Remediation Works 2026

eng: Limerick City and County Council proposes to undertake Fire Safety Remediation Works along with the provision of a stand alone modular building at Oak Lodge Hostel, Clare Street, Limerick. The purpose of the project is to address deficiencies identified within the Fire Risk Assessment, Fire Strategy Drawings and associated surveys and to improve the overall fire safety performance of the building. PROJECT DESCRIPTION New L1 Fire Detection and Alarm System, new Emergency Lighting System, replacement of all external windows and doors, AOV systems, replacement of internal doors, screens and ironmongery, fire stopping, compartmentation upgrades, fourth floor ceiling upgrade, attic insulation, associated builders works, decoration, testing and certification. Externally the provision of a stand-alone modular building to act as a recreational area.

description-proc.eng: Limerick City and County Council proposes to undertake Fire Safety Remediation Works along with the provision of a stand alone modular building at Oak Lodge Hostel, Clare Street, Limerick. The purpose of the project is to address deficiencies identified within the Fire Risk Assessment, Fire Strategy Drawings and associated surveys and to improve the overall fire safety performance of the building. PROJECT DESCRIPTION New L1 Fire Detection and Alarm System, new Emergency Lighting System, replacement of all external windows and doors, AOV systems, replacement of internal doors, screens and ironmongery, fire stopping, compartmentation upgrades, fourth floor ceiling upgrade, attic insulation, associated builders works, decoration, testing and certification. Externally the provision of a stand-alone modular building to act as a recreational area.

title-proc.eng: MetroLink – Environmental Monitoring Services

eng: Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) intends to procure independent environmental monitoring services in support of the MetroLink Programme. The M160 Environmental Monitoring Contract will establish a robust, continuous and auditable environmental monitoring regime to support statutory compliance, environmental protection and stakeholder assurance throughout the lifecycle of the M100 Advanced Works and the Main Contract Works. The contract will be procured as a NEC4 Term Service Contract using the Negotiated Procedure with Prior Call for Competition pursuant to SI 286/2016. All organisations wishing to participate in the procurement for "MetroLink – Environmental Monitoring Services” should register at Metrolink e-Sourcing Portal https://metrolink.app.jaggaer.com/ Upon the completion of the registration, please navigate to "PQQs/ITTs Open to All Suppliers" tab on the Main Dashboard, locate PQQ for “MetroLink – Environmental Monitoring Services", express an interest and submit a response. All clarification queries in relation to this procurement must be submitted via the Metrolink e-Sourcing portal.
Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII)

title-proc.eng: Rothe House: Archive and Collections Project

eng: This project will increase public access to the collections, archives and stories of Kilkenny through the creation of a visible collections store, enhanced archive facilities and improved research access within Rothe House. The existing Collection Store will be transformed from a closed storage area into a publicly accessible visible-storage space incorporating museum-standard storage bays, integrated object display areas, accessible drawers and a public research workspace. Museum-grade marmoleum flooring will be installed and new storage systems provided to improve both collection care and visitor access. A new public reading room will be created incorporating museum-standard archive shelving, storage and integrated display areas for material from the Kilkenny Archaeological Society library and archives. The project will also provide environmental monitoring equipment for the Collection Store, Reading Room and archive storage areas, plus photographic lightbox equipment and website infrastructure to support the ongoing digitisation of collections. Additional freestanding museum display cabinets will enable a greater proportion of the collection and archive material to be displayed and interpreted for visitors.
Rothe House Trust

title-proc.eng: 2024/36 - Readvertisement Year 3 of Panel for suitable Service Providers for the provision of Welding Training Courses and Demonstrations in 8 Lots

eng: LMETB established a panel for suitable Service Providers for the provision of Welding Training Course and Demonstrations in 8 Lots on 4th July 2024. This panel will run for 3 years until 3rd July 2027 and is open for applications during this period. The panel will be re-advertised on an annual basis. The purpose of this panel is to allow AMTCE source suitably qualified service providers to deliver Training programmes, from which service providers may be selected to participate in a mini competition for contract award for the design, demonstration, development, customisation, accreditation, delivery of training programmes once specific needs arise. LMETB is advertising on eTenders all its known, identified, potential programme, course categories identified and or run previously. This public procurement competition will be divided into Lots as described in tender documents. Applicants may apply for one or more lots. There is no restriction to the number of Lots you can apply for provided you meet the award criteria. The panel will be established for each Lot with a minimum of one provider subject to that number meeting the minimum criteria and rules.  Applications will be accepted by email to procurement@lmetb.ie with the following subject heading: Application for Panel Membership for the Provision of Welding Training Courses and Demonstration.
Louth and Meath Education and Training Board 1384

title-proc.gle: Services to deliver uplands farming demonstration and monitoring pilot programme.
title-proc.eng: Services to deliver uplands farming demonstration and monitoring pilot programme.

gle: Services to deliver uplands farming demonstration and monitoring pilot programme.
eng: Wild Atlantic Nature LIFE IP is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified service provider to deliver a one-year comprehensive Upland Monitoring and Demonstration Pilot Programme for assessing and demonstrating good practice in upland farms. Depending on progress in this period, it is envisaged to expand to a further 2 years. This initiative is supported through public funding from the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM), and includes Shared Island Initiative funding via the National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS). It aims to support the development of sustainable upland farming systems through monitoring, demonstration and knowledge transfer. To meet the objectives of the Shared Island Initiative, the proposed project should include close liaison with agriculture stakeholders in Northern Ireland. The programme will act as a proof of concept to inform future scaling and development of a longer-term initiative.

description-proc.eng: This Contract Award Notice is acting as a Modification Notice under Article 72 of 2014/24/EU to CFT 3109037 Contract for Darndale Park Waste Removal and Wall Construction to Breffni Building and Civil Engineering. Description of the procurement at the time of conclusion of the contract: The Contract comprises clearance and removal of approximately 40,000 tonnes of illegally dumped waste material and construction of boundary treatments and 117m of new 2.5m high precast boundary wall and footpath between Darndale Park and a group of Traveller Accommodation site known as the Northern Sites on the north side of Dublin within the boundaries of Darndale and Priorswood. The works shall include site clearance, removal of all waste material (investigations suggest non-hazardous), removal of asbestos, removal of end-of-life vehicles and other electrical goods, treatment and removal of invasive species, construction of concrete boundary walls, construction of new footpath, environmental monitoring. There is a requirement for removal of hazardous waste should it be encountered. Temporary works shall include construction of a construction stage haul road through Darndale Park to provide site access and all associated reinstatement works, protection to all existing services, fencing of works areas etc. Design of temporary works shall form part of the works. Changes arose in the following areas which were instructed in accordance with the provisions of the Public Works Contract - Removal and disposal of additional waste - Removal and disposal of horse carcass, contaminated waste, oil - Removal and disposal of large amount of historic concealed waste - Filling of excavated area with Article 27 backfill - Continued delays due to local obstruction of drainage construction - Construction of a new watermain that burst during excavation for drainage - Extensions of time under contract

title-proc.eng: Annual Readvertisement of Qualification System for the Purchase and or Leasing of Buses and Coaches for Bus Éireann/Irish Bus - (Annual Readvertisement 3/8 - Amended)

eng: Bus Éireann intends to procure low emission coaches and schools buses, and where possible zero-emission coaches with low environmental impact in compliance with the latest EURO VI Regulation. The vehicles will comply, as appropriate, with the EPA’s guidelines on road transport vehicles and the European Communities (Clean and Energy Efficient Road Transport Vehicles) (Amendment) Regulations 2021. To be considered for inclusion on a Qualification Panel(s), applicants must complete the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ) providing relevant details in relation to the criteria set out below for assessment. It is envisaged that this qualification system will be used to either purchase and or lease during the five-year term of the Qualification System. Economic operators apply once to qualify onto the panel by providing details of their financial and technical capacity against predefined published Selection Criteria within a PQQ. The Qualification Panel for the Purchase and or Lease of Buses and Coaches will be broken down in to sub categories called Lot 1 – Purchase of Buses and Coaches Expressway, and Lot 2 – Lease of Buses and Coaches Expressway, Lot 3 - Purchase of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 4 - Lease of School Buses and Coaches, Lot 5 - Purchase of single or double deck city bus type vehicles and Lot 6 - Lease of single or double deck city bus type vehicles. Economic operators can apply for the Lot(s) that best reflect their commercial operations. Economic operators must complete a PQQ for the Lot(s) that they wish to qualify to. Only economic operators who satisfy the selection criteria of each individual Lot will qualify on to that Lot. After the initial advertisement, the panel must be advertised annually for the duration of the panel (5 years) to continually inform the market place of its existence. Economic Operators can apply to qualify on to the panel, throughout the duration of the panel. Economic Operators who are already qualified to the panel can also amend their application at any interval should their financial or technical capacity or capability change. Qualifying onto a panel does not guarantee any work and/or contracts to a supplier. There is no obligation to use the Qualification Panel and contracts can be advertised on an individual basis using the Negotiated Procedure. (Annual Readvertisement 3/8 - Amended)

title-proc.eng: 2024/37 - Readvertisement Year 3 of Panel for suitable Service Providers for the provision of Environmental and Energy Management Training Courses and Demonstration in 2 Lots

eng: LMETB established a panel from which it will source suitably qualified service providers to deliver Training programmes, from which service providers may be selected to participate in a mini competition for contract award for the design, demonstration, development ,customisation, accreditation, delivery of training programmes once specific needs arise. LMETB is advertising all its known, identified, potential programme, courses identified and run previously. This public procurement competition will be divided into Lots as described in the tender documents. Applicants may apply for one or more lots. There is no restriction to the number of Lots you can apply for provided you meet the award criteria. The Panel has been established 12th July 2024 and will run for 3 years until 11th July 2027. Applications will be accepted via email to procurement@lmetb.ie with the following subject heading: Application for Panel Membership for the provision of Environmental and Energy Management Training Courses and Demonstration in 2 Lots.
Louth and Meath Education and Training Board 1384

title-proc.eng: Exhibition Design, Manufacture and Fit-Out Services for Donegal Famine Heritage Centre CLG (trading as The Workhouse), Dunfanaghy, Co. Donegal

eng: The Donegal Famine Heritage Centre CLG (trading as 'The Workhouse') seeks to appoint a suitably qualified service provider to deliver the final design, production, and fit-out of a modern museum exhibition at The Workhouse, Dunfanaghy, Co. Donegal. Project Context and Funding The Workhouse, Dunfanaghy has been awarded grant funding by Failte Ireland through the Coast-to-Coast Capital Investment Scheme. This project is a cornerstone of the organisation's strategy, which aims to quintuple visitor numbers and revenue by transforming the site into a premier, year round, all weather destination on the Wild Atlantic Way. Core Deliverables: The Service Provider will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of the exhibition, including: Final Interpretive and Spatial Design: Utilising the provided Draft Interpretive Plan and Content Framework to develop a high-quality, universally accessible visitor journey across an envisaged five distinct zones. This includes proposing a creative repositioned layout for internal partition walls to optimise visitor flow, maximising physical wall space, and the design, off-site fabrication, and installation of a detailed, historically accurate physical scale model of the original Workhouse building and grounds to serve as a central interpretive anchor. Content and Language Management: Collaborating closely with the Workhouse Working Group to edit and finalise all exhibition scripts. Deliverables include fully bilingual (English and Irish/Gaeilge) printed and digital displays to ensure strict compliance with the Official Languages (Amendment) Act 2021, alongside a professionally recorded four-language self-guided audio tour delivered via both proprietary devices and web-hosted smartphone frameworks. Technological Integration: Procuring, programming, installing, and commissioning all multimedia and audio-visual (AV) elements. This includes immersive digital media treatments and a dedicated, high-capacity Digital Archive Explorer interactive kiosk. Physical Fit-Out, Enabling Works and Heating Upgrades: Managing the complete site preparation, including the safe demolition and lawful disposal off-site of legacy exhibition fixtures. Physical works include constructing agreed internal partition walls, executing all necessary first/second-fix electrical, and decorative trades, and installing a centralised ambient climate monitoring display (in reception area). The Service Provider must also supply and commission an active, humidity control solution (with a total prohibition on external stone wall penetrations) and supply and commission a modern, energy-efficient heating upgrade compliant with Regulation (EU) 2024/1103 for the exhibition space. Please note that all works, installations, and commissioning under this contract must be fully completed, validated, and handed over to the Contracting Authority by no later than 30th March 2027.

description-proc.eng: Gas Networks Ireland (GNI) is establishing a Qualification System for the provision of Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) works and services (Lot 1) and Operation and Maintenance (O&M) services (Lot 2) for the Strategic Gas Emergency Reserve (SGER). Lot 1 is for the engineering, procurement, and construction works and services to complete infrastructure assets including but not limited the jetty, trestle, topside structures, pipelines, above ground installation (AGI), integration with FSRU, onshore terminal systems, related ancillary and enabling utilities to site and the management of nominated subcontractor(s). Applicants who are interested in participating in the Initial Competition must submit their QSQ responses through the eTenders system by 12.00hrs (Irish time) 18th September 2026, unless amended.

title-proc.eng: Historic Mines Services 2026

eng: Lot 1 Monitoring Services: Environmental, geotechnical and geoheritage monitoring of Avoca and Silvermines. To include: • Reviews of conceptual flow model, monitoring objectives and monitoring network integrity at the sites; • Twice a year environmental monitoring including surface water, groundwater and dust; • Annual geotechnical and geoheritage monitoring.

Lot 2 Critical Failure Assessment: Assess nature, effects and mitigation of dam breach at Gortmore and Shelton Abbey Tailings Management Facilities. To include: • Geotechnical review of site characterisation data • Critical Failure Assessment including: Risk assessment including credible failure scenarios; dam breach modelling and consequence classification. • Emergency preparedeness response plan (EPRP) for dam failure. • Expert Final Report & Regulatory Presentations. • Design for interim early warning system for embankment failure at Gortmore TMF. • Review of CFM and ERP after three years, or after substantive changes to the condition of the site (incidental or due to remediation works).

Lot 3 Risk inventory: National inventory, risk assessment and prioritisation of physical risks at approx. 138 historic mine sites nationwide. To include: • Desk study on each site using available information. • Physical risk inspection and surveys of surface features at all sites. • Development of inventory, assessment and prioritisation scheme. • Report and GIS maps.
Department of Climate Energy and the Environment

title-proc.eng: The provision of Eirevo Metro Ethernet Links for Trinity College Dublin

eng: "The contracting authority intends to continue procuring metropolitan connectivity services from Eir (eirevro) for a limited period while a strategic review and phased replacement programme is undertaken. The existing services are delivered over proprietary legacy infrastructure that cannot be replicated through a straightforward like-for-like procurement. Replacement would require significant redesign, capital investment, construction and migration activities, together with detailed assessment of operational resilience requirements. To ensure continuity of service and avoid risks to critical operational sites, the authority considers it necessary to maintain the existing Eir services while developing and implementing a future connectivity strategy over a period of approximately four to five years. This approach will facilitate a controlled migration to modern connectivity solutions following completion of the required technical, operational and financial evaluations."

title-proc.eng: Environmental Monitoring System for the National Children's Hospital Ireland

eng: The services comprise implementation of an end-to-end Environmental Monitoring System for the new children's hospital, to be operated by Children's Health Ireland (CHI). As CHI prepares for the opening of the National Children’s Hospital Ireland (NCHI), the organisation has identified the need to develop a comprehensive Independent Environmental Monitoring system. This system will serve CHI at the NCHI and potentially the satellite facilities at CHI at Tallaght and CHI at Connolly. The system will be specifically for use in a hospital environment monitoring pharmacies, lab and speciality environments and Temperatures. The system must ensure compliance with suitable ISO accreditation standards and integrate with a centralised monitoring system that meets current environmental and temperature monitoring standards. Any contract award will be subject to funding approval.
Children's Health Ireland (CHI)
Medical Supply Company Ltd

title-proc.eng: An Area Monitoring System Service

eng: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is issuing this tender competition to enter into a contract with a vendor to supply an Area Monitoring System (AMS) Service within DAFM which has the capacity to deliver the obligations of Article 70 of Regulation 2021/2116 which requires the continued delivery of an AMS service. Article 65 of 2021/2116 defines an area monitoring system as a procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data of at least equivalent value. It is the intent of this tender competition to solicit proposals from all interested vendors possessing expertise to provide an AMS solution to accommodate the needs of the Area Monitoring and Land Systems Division, within the guidelines established in the tender documents.
Department of Agriculture Food and the Marine

description-proc.eng: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is issuing this tender competition to enter into a contract with a vendor to supply an Area Monitoring System (AMS) Service within DAFM which has the capacity to deliver the obligations of Article 70 of Regulation 2021/2116 which requires the continued delivery of an AMS service. Article 65 of 2021/2116 defines an area monitoring system as a procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data of at least equivalent value. It is the intent of this tender competition to solicit proposals from all interested vendors possessing expertise to provide an AMS solution to accommodate the needs of the Area Monitoring and Land Systems Division, within the guidelines established in the tender documents.

title-proc.eng: 9947 Station Services Mediation System (SSMS)

eng: Iarnród Éireann – Irish Rail (IÉ) is seeking to establish a contract for the design, supply, configuration, integration, commissioning, support and maintenance of a Station Services Mediation System (SSMS). The SSMS will provide the central processing, integration and management platform for real-time passenger information services across the Iarnród Éireann railway network. The system will interface with existing and future IÉ operational systems, including timetable systems, signalling systems, Passenger Information Display Systems (PIDS), Long Line Public Address (LLPA) systems and external passenger information platforms. The solution will support the phased migration from IÉ's existing Customer Information Systems to the future Centralised Traffic Control and Communications Based Interlocking (CBI) environment while maintaining continuity of passenger information services throughout the transition. The scope includes all necessary software, licences, configuration and integration services, testing, commissioning, migration, documentation, training, maintenance, technical support, cybersecurity updates, lifecycle and obsolescence management required to provide a fully operational and supported SSMS solution. The proposed contract will be for an initial period of eight (8) years, with an option for IÉ to extend the contract for a further three (3) years at its discretion.
Iarnród Eireann-Irish Rail

title-proc.eng: Fire Remediation Works at Rowantree Court, Mullaghmonaghan, Monaghan

eng: The project involves the execution of fire remediation works to an existing 24-unit residential development located at Rowantree Court, Mullaghmonaghan, Monaghan, on behalf of the client, Oaklee Housing. The objective of the works is to address identified fire safety deficiencies in order to bring the building into compliance with current fire protection and life safety standards outlined in TGD Part B (Fire Safety) of the Building Regulations and other relevant codes such as IS 3218:2913 for fire alarm systems. The scope of the remediation works includes, but is not limited to: • Installation of fire-stopping systems at service penetrations and wall/floor junctions. • Replacement or upgrade of fire-rated doors, closers, and seals to comply with TGD-B. • Retrofitting of cavity barriers at floor levels in external cavity. • Fire alarm cable rerouting and improvements to service risers and shafts. • Sealing of socket/switch boxes within fire-rated partitions. • General improvement of compartmentation and passive fire protection measures. All works will be undertaken within a live residential environment, requiring a high level of coordination to minimise disruption to residents.
Oaklee Housing

title-proc.eng: Multi-Party Framework Agreement for Minor Building Works Residential for Tipperary County Council

eng: This is the Stage 1 process for the Establishment of a Multi-Party Framework Agreement for Minor Building Works Residential for Tipperary County Council. Further details will be provided at stage 2 of the process for tenderers who qualify to Stage 2. This initial Stage 1 is to determine tenderers who are suitably qualified to be added to this framework. Typically, the value of each Works Contract will range from 25k to approximately 400k. This framework has the potential to be established for 4years estimated from early Jan 2027 until end Dec 2030. The scope of the Framework will include any building works which may be required within any of the 5no. Municipal Districts of County Tipperary; 1. Nenagh District 2. Templemore-Thurles District 3. Cahir, Cashel, Tipperary District 4. Clonmel District 5. Carrick-on-Suir District. Works within this Framework may include but are not limited to general repairs, maintenance to the building fabric, roofing works, modifications for disability access, internal external modification and alterations to buildings, electrical works, plumbing, heating and mechanical system works, replacement of windows and internal and external doors, installation modification kitchens, floor coverings, painting and decorating, suspended ceiling works, dry‐lining, jointing and plastering, construction of small extensions, minor demolition works, clearance works in preparation for re‐letting re‐occupation, external site works such as driveways, steps, paths, fences and boundary walls, landscaping, drainage and residential waste and foul water treatment works. Dwellings Buildings may or may not be occupied.
Tipperary County Council

title-proc.eng: An Area Monitoring System Service

eng: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is issuing this tender competition to enter into a contract with a vendor to supply an Area Monitoring System (AMS) Service within DAFM which has the capacity to deliver the obligations of Article 70 of Regulation 2021/2116 which requires the continued delivery of an AMS service. Article 65 of 2021/2116 defines an area monitoring system as a procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data of at least equivalent value. It is the intent of this tender competition to solicit proposals from all interested vendors possessing expertise to provide an AMS solution to accommodate the needs of the Area Monitoring and Land Systems Division, within the guidelines established in the tender documents.
Department of Agriculture Food and the Marine

description-proc.eng: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is issuing this tender competition to enter into a contract with a vendor to supply an Area Monitoring System (AMS) Service within DAFM which has the capacity to deliver the obligations of Article 70 of Regulation 2021/2116 which requires the continued delivery of an AMS service. Article 65 of 2021/2116 defines an area monitoring system as a procedure of regular and systematic observation, tracking and assessment of agricultural activities and practices on agricultural areas by Copernicus Sentinels satellite data or other data of at least equivalent value. title-proc.eng: Supply of Keys to Bus Éireann

eng: This tender is for the supply of keys to Bus Éireann on an as-required basis. The requirement includes, but is not limited to, ignition keys, entrance door keys, luggage compartment keys, emergency access keys, security keys, service and maintenance keys, fuel access keys, and passenger facility keys. A list of key types, part numbers, vehicle applications, and estimated annual quantities is provided within the Pricing Schedule. The keys supplied shall provide full functional compatibility with the associated Bus Éireann fleet vehicles, equipment, lockers, compartments, security systems, and facilities for which they are intended. The successful Supplier shall be capable of providing OEM-compatible or equivalent keys and, where required, producing keys from existing samples, key codes, or other information provided by Bus Éireann. All items shall be delivered directly to Bus Éireann depots and garages nationwide as required.
Bus Eireann/Irish Bus

description-proc.eng: This tender is for the supply of keys to Bus Éireann on an as-required basis. The requirement includes, but is not limited to, ignition keys, entrance door keys, luggage compartment keys, emergency access keys, security keys, service and maintenance keys, fuel access keys, and passenger facility keys. A list of key types, part numbers, vehicle applications, and estimated annual quantities is provided within the Pricing Schedule. The keys supplied shall provide full functional compatibility with the associated Bus Éireann fleet vehicles, equipment, lockers, compartments, security systems, and facilities for which they are intended. The successful Supplier shall be capable of providing OEM-compatible or equivalent keys and, where required, producing keys from existing samples, key codes, or other information provided by Bus Éireann. All items shall be delivered directly to Bus Éireann depots and garages nationwide as required.

title-proc.eng: EM 06/26 - Fire Management Services Framework

eng: Expressions of interest are invited from suitably qualified Applicants interested in being considered for the provision of Fire Management Services which will deliver a comprehensive, integrated fire safety solution across the entire Contracting Entities business. The Contracting Entity intends to establish a multi supplier Framework Agreement, for the provision of requirements listed below but is not limited to and will be divided into the following Lots. • Lot 1: Fire Detection and Emergency Systems o Fire Detection, Emergency Lighting and Fire Alarm Systems Routine inspection, testing, and preventative maintenance of all fire alarm systems. Fault diagnosis, repair, and system upgrades where required Certification in line with applicable standards 24/7 call-out and emergency response capability. • Lot 2: Fire Suppression Systems o Fire Extinguishers, Fire Blankets - Supply, installation, inspection, testing, and maintenance of all portable fire extinguishers. Refilling, replacement, and disposal in accordance with regulatory requirements. Asset tagging and tracking to ensure compliance and traceability o Fire Hose Reels and Hydrants - Inspection, testing, and maintenance of fire hose reels and hydrant systems pressure testing. • Lot 3: Sprinkler Systems Sprinkler Systems – Service, installation, inspection, testing and maintenance of Sprinkler systems. These services must ensure full compliance with all relevant fire safety legislation, standards, and best practices, supporting a wide range of operational environments including landfilling activities, bog operations, and Edenderry Power Plant facilities.

title-proc.eng: UCDOPP5616 Request for Tender for Supply Installation Commissioning and Maintenance of Dual Inlet Isotope Ratio Mass Spectrometer System

eng: The UCD School of Earth Sciences requires a Dual Inlet Isotope Ratio Mass Spectrometry System. This equipment will be central to the development of a new dissolved gas tracer laboratory at UCD that is being established to support a recently awarded European Research Council project. The project aims to apply new highprecision dissolved-gas and isotope tracers to understand physical and biogeochemical processes in groundwater systems over timescales ranging from decades to centuries.
University College Dublin ( UCD )

title-proc.eng: The Supply of 1 x 6 Seater Vehicle

eng: The Supply of 1 x 6 Seater Vehicle Kare invites you to provide a tender for the provision of the following.  1 x second hand Vehicle (e.g. Ford Custom, Volkswagen Caddy or similar type) See vehicle specification Table A  The vehicle Must be able to be driven by a person holding a B class driving license.  Tenders to outline costs of vehicles inclusive of VAT and any other taxes or charges applicable to the vehicle.  Kare reserves the right to choose a supplier based on the availability of vehicles to view and purchase efficiently. All purchases are subject to the funding available Vs the costs received.  You MUST clearly specify the timelines / lead times involved with the purchase / of the vehicle outlined.  We will require evidence of the registration of the second-hand vehicle to confirm their immediate availability.  When evaluating the suitability of the vehicle, we will award scores based on the year of the vehicle, the kilometrage and the suitability for our needs. We will view the vehicle in person, to assess its suitability. We will also have the vehicle inspected by a qualified mechanic to verify the quality of the vehicle. Please refer to the images below as an example of what our requirements are.  NOTE - All vehicles to be taxed for a minimum of 3 months upon delivery to Kare.

title-proc.eng: Consultancy Services to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case for an Irish language based sports and community centre for CLG Na Gaeil Óga, Leamhcán (Lucan), Baile Átha Cliath

eng: Na Gaeil Óga CLG organises more than 1,000 Irish language based events each year for participants aged 3 years and upwards. These include sports training, games, workshops, social and cultural events, Irish classes and parent and toddler activities. The club has 500 active members. At present, the club rents various facilities such as grass-based pitches, all-weather pitches, halls, gyms, ball walls and meeting rooms in Lucan and the surrounding areas to host its activities. The club’s members feel that a centrally located facility, managed by the club, would provide many advantages in terms of the development of both the club and the Irish language in the area. The club intends to engage a consultant to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case in accordance with the Infrastructure Guidelines issued by the Department of Public Expenditure, National Development Plan Delivery and Reform and as further detailed in the tender documents to support capital funding applications to various Government departments into the future. The club will be applying to An Roinn Forbartha Tuaite agus Pobail agus Gaeltachta for funding to undertake the Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case.
Na Gaeil Óga CLG

title-proc.eng: Open Competition for the School of Business Student Feedback Software System 529

eng: The Maynooth University School of Business was established in 2007 and currently employs over 100 academic, administrative, and support staff as well as a student body of over 4,000 full time undergraduate and postgraduate students. The School of Business offers a range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and PhD programmes across a wide range of business disciplines as well as offering a suite of modules within the Arts programme. The teaching and learning experience of our students involves a series of face-to-face lectures within our state-of-the-art facilities within Maynooth’s campus delivered primarily by academic faculty but can also include guest lectures from industry. The School’s collective pedagogical strategy is further enhanced by Moodle, an online learning environment whereby learning materials, supplementary readings, case studies, or other media resources facilitating additional student engagement with individual modules. description-proc.eng: The Maynooth University School of Business was established in 2007 and currently employs over 100 academic, administrative, and support staff as well as a student body of over 4,000 full time undergraduate and postgraduate students. The School of Business offers a range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and PhD programmes across a wide range of business disciplines as well as offering a suite of modules within the Arts programme. The teaching and learning experience of our students involves a series of face-to-face lectures within our state-of-the-art facilities within Maynooth’s campus delivered primarily by academic faculty but can also include guest lectures from industry. The School’s collective pedagogical strategy is further enhanced by Moodle, an online learning environment whereby learning materials, supplementary readings, case studies, or other media resources facilitating additional student engagement with individual modules. title-proc.eng: Dublin City Council Single Party Framework Agreement for an Integrated Design Team for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project

eng: The Contracting Authority, Dublin City Council, intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a Integrated Design Team to deliver planning, engineering, environmental, stakeholder engagement and other specialist consultancy services for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project (CFDPRP). The Project is located along the Clontarf waterfront in Dublin and encompasses a highly sensitive coastal environment adjoining designated European sites, including Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA). The Project has been initiated to address existing and future coastal and surface water flood risks while delivering a coordinated programme of public realm enhancement, active travel improvements and environmental benefits. The scheme shall be developed through an integrated design approach that balances flood resilience, climate adaptation, biodiversity, heritage, placemaking, sustainable mobility, environmental protection and stakeholder aspirations. The initial call-off contract under the Framework will require the successful Applicant to undertake all services necessary to develop the Project from commencement through option identification, scheme development, environmental assessment, statutory consent processes and detailed design. This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 8969388 – Input when notice created . Please note that this project is subject to funding.
Dublin City Council

title-proc.eng: UL1063 Multi Supplier Framework for the provision of Meeting Booths to the University of Limerick

eng: The University of Limerick (UL) is seeking to establish a sustainable Multi-Supplier Framework Agreement for modular Acoustic Booths/Meeting Pods available in both solo and multi‑person configurations to meet the requirements of any department of UL. Requirements include: • supply of modular acoustic pods; delivery, installation and commissioning on site • integrated LED lighting, power module (e.g. 230V, RJ45, USB, USB-C) and ventilation, with optional presence/motion sensors • high‑grade acoustic panel insulation • optional internal table or worksurface • optional seating • optional mount for screen installation • stable installation Booths must be constructed using EU fire-safe materials, safety rated laminated or acoustic panels - including compliant fabrics and acoustic panels, and must offer a range of fabric/finish options to suit Library interiors. A minimum warranty period and reliable after‑sales support are required. Depending on configuration options may need to include a wheelchair‑accessible layout with suitable door width, low threshold access and appropriate internal clearances.

title-proc.eng: DCC Single Party Framework Agreement for the Supply, Installation, Maintenance, Removal and Storage of Artistic Lighting Illuminations and Associated Equipment

eng: Dublin City Council intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a suitably qualified service provider to deliver an initial contract for the Dublin Winter Lights Festival. The Dublin Winter Lights Festival has traditionally taken place primarily in outdoor venues and will continue to do so, while also exploring the idea of having some indoor experiences in 2027 and future years. Dublin City Council’s Dublin Winter Lights Festival has illuminated iconic landmarks and more unconventional locations previously, using a range of different projection methods, with more recent years seeing a trend towards full digital projections with locations such as the GPO, Custom House and Collins Barracks seeing full digital video mapping animations. By consistently seeking out innovative and unexpected sites, the festival has continued to evolve and stay fresh. It combines digital art, lighting design, and public performance to illuminate key cultural landmarks across the city, Note: the subject matter of this procurement relates to Title III Services as defined in Directive 2014/24/EU. Please note that this project is subject to funding. The framework agreement will be for a period of six (6) years. The Contracting Authority considers a framework term of six (6) years necessary due to the specialist nature of the services and the significant investment required by the successful Framework Member in artistic lighting infrastructure, projection equipment, storage facilities, specialist personnel, festival development and stakeholder relationships. The longer framework duration is intended to facilitate continuity of service, enable long-term planning and programming of the Dublin City Council Dublin Winter Lights Festival, support the development of artistic partnerships and innovation, and provide value for money through the amortisation of equipment and mobilisation costs over a longer period. The framework will also support the ongoing maintenance, storage and reuse of lighting infrastructure and associated equipment, contributing to sustainability objectives and reducing lifecycle costs. The duration is therefore justified by the subject matter of the framework and the need to secure consistent, high-quality delivery of a flagship cultural event and related artistic lighting projects. The Contracting Authority confirms that the period of any contracts awarded under the framework agreement may extend beyond the date of expiry of the agreement. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID xxxxxxx – Input when notice created

title-proc.eng: Collection and Disposal of Category 1 Waste from Dublin Airport Passenger Terminals and Airside Stables

eng: Due to the risk of introducing diseases into the European Union (EU) from third countries, there are strict rules and regulations around animal products and plants and plant products entering the EU. Any products that are prohibited from entry are seized and disposed of as Category 1 waste. Prohibited products in passengers’ luggage on airplanes poses a very particular risk to public, animal and plant health, resulting in its disposal being strictly regulated. Accordingly, there are controls are in place to ensure that seizures of prohibited food or plants at Dublin Airport is controlled and disposed of in a manner that minimises risk to public, animal and plant health. Past outbreaks of diseases (e.g. Foot and Mouth Disease) demonstrate the risks posed by products of animal origin, animal by-products (ABP) and plants being introduced to Ireland through travel. The successful tenderer will be responsible for the removal, emptying, cleaning and disinfection of the Department of Agriculture, Food and Marine bins at following locations in Dublin Airport: • Terminal One • Terminal Two • Airside Stables It must be noted the successful tenderer must be registered to land Category 1 waste under Article 23 of Regulation (EC) 1069/2009 and must be registered prior to commencing operations. The operator must also ensure to abide by all relevant requirements set out in national (SI 187 2014) and EU Legislation (Regulations 1069/2009 and 142/2011). Full details in Notice titled CN25ALander, published with the tender documents. Also please note there are Terms and Conditions from Dublin Airport Authority that the successful tenderer must comply with to operate at the airport, please refer to "Dublin Airport Authority miscellaneous charges booklet 2026" published with the tender documents.
Department of Agriculture Food and the Marine

title-proc.eng: Open Competition for the Provision of Student Placement Software 539

eng: Maynooth University is seeking to procure a robust and configurable software solution to manage professional practice placements across its professionally regulated programmes. The management of these placements is a complex, multi-stakeholder process spanning the Schools of Nursing, Applied Social Studies and Education departments, with approximately 1,750 students placed annually across a wide range of local and national settings. This activity is supported by a substantial tutor cohort - approximately 500 in Nursing, 150 in Education, and 150 in Applied Social Studies — each requiring reliable tools to oversee and assess student progress. In addition to coordinating placement logistics, the University must meet the record-keeping requirements set by professional regulatory bodies, including detailed documentation of each student's placement site, hours completed, assessment strategies, and site evaluations. The University is therefore inviting tenders for new software to provide an effective, efficient, and scalable platform capable of managing the full lifecycle of professional practice placements across these diverse disciplines.
Maynooth University

title-proc.eng: PRE-QUALIFICATION QUESTIONNAIRE (PQQ) for Design, Build, Manufacture and Installation of Adaptable Educational Workstation Frames for TU Dublin

eng: For the purposes of this PQQ, the requirement is for the supply and installation of up to 64 Adaptable Educational Workstation Frames, comprising 32 units for North House Building and 32 units for Premier House Building. The final configuration will vary depending on the final floor layouts. It is anticipated that the Plaza layout will consist of four rows of eight workstations, with the two external rows requiring rear sliding-door access and the two central rows configured back-to-back without rear access doors. The design may also need to accommodate existing structural features, including pillars, within North House Building. At present, no equivalent configuration or floor layout has been developed for Premier House Building. The successful tenderer(s) will be required to work collaboratively with the project design team during the dialogue phase to establish the most appropriate Adaptable Educational Workstation Frame configuration and layout for Premier House Building, taking account of operational requirements and any site-specific constraints.
Technological University Dublin (TU Dublin)

title-proc.eng: Provision of Managed Business Process Support Services for CORU

eng: The objective of this tender is to implement a workforce augmentation facility where the awarded tenderer will provide additional resources to CORU to process applications for recognition and registration applications. The objective is to progress and process these applications in a timely manner. The team will be reporting directly to a Senior Manager in CORU or their designate. Please note that all external resources will be trained in the application processes, SOPs and checklists, using a training pack developed by CORU. The supervisor and resources are to be based in Ireland so that they can attend face to face training as well as attend regular virtual team meetings.
Health and Social Care Professionals Council (CORU)

title-proc.eng: Request for Tenders for the Provision of a Rapid Evidence Assessment in relation to reading for pleasure among children and young people in Ireland with a particular focus on boys and young men

eng: The Department of Education and Youth is seeking research services from a suitably qualified contractor/s to conduct a rapid evidence review in relation to reading for pleasure among children and young people in Ireland, with a particular focus on boys and young men. For the purposes of this review, the terms children and young people and boys and young men refer to learners from the early learning and care (ELC) sector through primary and post-primary education. The review should therefore consider evidence relating to attitudes, engagement and participation in reading for pleasure across the continuum of educational provision, including key developmental and educational transition points.
Department of Education and Youth

title-proc.eng: Multi-Party Framework for Port Hydrographic Survey Works

eng: DPC intends to establish a multi-party framework for Port Hydrographic Survey Works, to: a. provide hydrographic, geophysical, and associated marine survey services across DPC’s operational and capital programme requirements; b. support DPC in fulfilling its statutory duties as a client in respect of health and safety coordination during the design process, across a range of civil, structural, marine, building and infrastructure projects throughout the framework term. Framework Members shall be capable of providing, as a minimum, the following survey services whether in-house or through an approved consortium: DPC requires firms with strong health and safety design coordination experience across a range of construction project types, including civil engineering, marine structures, port infrastructure, buildings, and utilities works. A. Core Survey Services Non-Exhaustive The required expertise includes, but is not limited to: • Multi-Beam EchoSounder MBES monitoring surveys of all navigation channels, berth facilities, docks, and anchorage areas; • MBES measurement surveys in association with capital and maintenance dredging works, including pre-, interim, and post-dredge surveys; • Assessment of seabed characteristic information from backscatter returns where MBES equipment is used; • Single-Beam EchoSounder SBES monitoring surveys where required, particularly at Dundalk Port and in shallow areas; • Assistance with archaeological and obstruction identification, including geophysical, magnetometer, side scan sonar SSS, and drop-down video DDV services; • Acquisition of intertidal areas and adjacent structures using LIDAR-based methods; • Establishment of new and existing berth fender lines and quay features; • Calibration and validation of port tide gauges and tide boards; • Establishment and/or validation of temporary benchmarks; • Provision of post-processing, quality control, and data management, including delivery of survey data in agreed formats XYZ, LAS, CARIS, PDF, and other formats as required; • Preparation of survey reports, cross-sections, contour plots, and comparison overlays to DPC’s requirements. • Professional indemnity, marine liability, and other insurances in the amounts required under the Framework Agreement. B. Additional Services In addition to the core survey services set out above, DPC may require Framework Members to provide the following additional services under individual call-off contracts: Additional services may include non-exhaustive: • Sub-bottom profiling surveys; • Wreck investigation and obstruction surveys; • Geotechnical sampling support positioning and data integration; • Assistance with environmental monitoring surveys suspended sediment, turbidity, etc.; • GNSS/RTK control network establishment and verification; BIM and GIS integration and delivery of survey data to DPC’s asset management systems. Candidates should note that this list is non-exhaustive, and the successful tenderer may be required to provide other survey services as requested by DPC during the Framework. Important: DPC seeks only Candidates capable of delivering all core services listed in Section 3.1A, whether in-house or through a consortium/grouping. Applications limited to one or more survey types only may be rejected.
Dublin Port Company_411

title-proc.eng: Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary

eng: Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. Tipperary County Council is undertaking a competitive tendering process for the establishment of a Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Multi-Disciplinary Consultancy Services for Public Realm, Landscape and Building Upgrade Projects in Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. The Framework Agreement will require the successful Consultant to provide, either directly or through its proposed multi-disciplinary team, all of the following services: 1. Architectural Services – Public Realm 2. Conservation Architectural Services 3. Landscape Architectural Services 4. Civil and Structural Engineering Services 5. Quantity Surveying Services 6. Project Management Services 7. Project Supervisor Design Process (PSDP) Services 8. Employer’s Representative Services 9. Public Liaison / Stakeholder Engagement Services 10. Mechanical and Electrical Engineering Services 11. Planning Services 12. Archaeological Services 13. Fire Engineering Services Only Applicants capable of providing all of the above disciplines and associated specialist expertise, whether in-house, through subcontractors or as part of a grouping/consortium, will be considered. This competition will be conducted using a restricted procedure. At Stage 1, Applicants will be assessed against the suitability and selection criteria set out in the Suitability Assessment Questionnaire. It is intended that the five highest-scoring Applicants, subject to a sufficient number meeting all minimum requirements and rules for selection, will be invited to participate in Stage 2. At Stage 2, shortlisted Applicants will be issued with the Invitation to Tender and associated tender documentation. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the award criteria and weightings set out in the Invitation to Tender. The highest-ranked compliant Tenderer will be appointed to the Single-Party Framework Agreement and will also be awarded the Initial Contract. The Initial Contract will relate to the further development and delivery of public realm and associated projects in Clonmel. Clonmel Town Centre requires a significant streetscape and public realm upgrade. A design previously received Part VIII approval; however, the design now requires further development, amendment and coordination to reflect the current project scope and available funding and to bring the project through detailed design, tender, construction and handover stages. Tipperary County Council has also acquired a protected structure for which design development and a Part VIII planning process will be required. The Architect-Led Design Team may therefore be required to deliver a combination of public realm, landscape, civil engineering and building upgrade works, including works to protected and heritage structures. The Architect will act as Lead Consultant and will be responsible for coordinating and managing the full multi-disciplinary design team, programme, cost and delivery of the projects. During the construction stage, the Design Team will be required to provide ongoing technical support, respond to queries arising on site and advise on proposed variations and other matters affecting the delivery of the works. Projects arising under the Framework Agreement are anticipated to be funded, in whole or in part, through the Towns and Cities Regeneration Investment Fund (TCRIF) and/or other available funding programmes. Please note that an ITT is not required for this stage of the tender process.
Tipperary County Council

Over the course of the framework agreement, it is envisioned that the successful framework member may be required to provide alternative promotional material, depending upon need. It is anticipated that the items in question will feature the Hospital’s logo, in single colour, as set out in the Tender documents, together with a phone number, e-mail address and potentially a brief slogan.

title-proc.eng: Supply, Delivery, Installation and Commissioning of Gelato Production and Refrigeration Equipment - Nice Ice Cream / NOBLE

eng: Alexander Kuzminov trading as Nice Ice Cream, operating under the NOBLE brand, invites tenders for the supply, delivery, installation and commissioning of equipment for the expansion and modernisation of its artisan gelato and sorbet production facility at Unit 3, An Chistin Food Hub, Castlerea, Co. Roscommon, F45 R6F5, Ireland. The procurement comprises four lots: 1. Gelato production, fruit and berry processing, and blast freezing equipment. 2. Three professional refrigerated gelato service carts, for fixed-position operation during service. 3. Chocolate and premium ingredient processing equipment, including one melanger/refiner, an automatic tempering machine with vibrating table, a chocolate melter and a cocoa-butter incubation/crystallisation unit. 4. A modular walk-in freezer room with a normal storage setpoint of -25°C. Tenderers may tender for one, several or all lots. Each lot must be offered as a complete, independently priced supply and will be evaluated separately. One supplier may be awarded all lots if successful in each relevant evaluation and capable of delivering the combined scope. Equivalent solutions meeting the published functional and mandatory requirements are permitted. Prices must include the mandatory equipment and accessories, freight, unloading, positioning, installation and equipment-side connections within the specified scope, commissioning, operator training, conformity documentation, warranty and after-sales support in Ireland. Tenderers must clearly identify any purchaser-provided utility or building works and the boundaries of their installation responsibilities. The detailed RFT and lot schedules govern the requirements. Questions and tenders must be submitted through the appropriate eTenders facilities. The project is proposed for LEADER assistance. Contract formation and commencement are subject to funding approval, applicable grant permissions and the purchaser's written authorisation, as set out in the RFT.

title-proc.eng: CFT to establish a To establish a Multi-Supplier Framework Agreement for the Provision of Recruitment Services – Executive Search, General and Specialist Recruitment

eng: Through the establishment of a multi-party framework agreement ("Framework Agreement"), the successful tenderer(s) ("Framework Members") will be required to work with Research Ireland in the sourcing, assessment, selection and placement activities as described in detail in Appendix 1 to this CFT “Requirements and Specifications” for a diverse range of roles that arise across Research Ireland. Research Ireland invites tenders for the establishment of a Multi-Supplier Framework Agreement for the provision of recruitment and personnel placement services across the organisation, including executive search, general recruitment and specialist recruitment, and encompassing permanent, fixed-term/specified-purpose and temporary staffing requirements. The Framework Agreement will replace the current Framework Agreement for recruitment services. title-proc.eng: TR5389 Service Provider to provide Digital workspace Monitoring Software

eng: The Contracting Entity intends to procure a contract for a Service Provider to provide, licence, support and maintenance for ESB’s Digital workspace Monitoring Software. ESB operates the ControlUp monitoring software which enables us to leverage modern digital technologies to gather and analyse data at every critical point of our Digital Workspace infrastructure. It also provides historical data that is very important for recognising trends and proactively addressing issues. It is proposed that the Contract will include (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): ControlUp Performance Monitoring Software The supply of software support with licensing for the existing ESB Digital Workspace solution. Maintenance for all existing software. Management of software licences/subscriptions for all devices and software modules is required. The supply of software support with licensing for any new software added during the term of the contract. This will not be restricted to ControlUp related products as other digital monitoring solutions will be considered.
Electricity Supply Board ( ESB )

title-proc.eng: The Provision of Fluid Warmers and All Related Consumables

eng: The Contracting Authority intends to award a contract for the supply and support of Medical Grade Fluid warmers and their corresponding consumables. The Contracting Authority requires highly reliable, safety-tested fluid warming technologies. It is a requirement that the equipment must perform accurately across a range of clinical environments and must accommodate varying clinical demands ranging from routine, low-flow continuous infusions to high-volume, rapid trauma requirements. A contract of four years’ duration shall be awarded for the provision of thirty fluid warmers, any required attachments, including all support, maintenance, repair and replacement of the equipment and the supply of all sterile single use consumables. The Contracting Authority shall remunerate the successful tenderer for the provision of the required equipment through the purchase of sterile single use consumables.
