description-proc.eng: The Contracting Authority intends to award a contract for the supply and support of Medical Grade Fluid warmers and their corresponding consumables. The Contracting Authority requires highly reliable, safety-tested fluid warming technologies. It is a requirement that the equipment must perform accurately across a range of clinical environments and must accommodate varying clinical demands ranging from routine, low-flow continuous infusions to high-volume, rapid trauma requirements. A contract of four years’ duration shall be awarded for the provision of thirty fluid warmers, any required attachments, including all support, maintenance, repair and replacement of the equipment and the supply of all sterile single use consumables. The Contracting Authority shall remunerate the successful tenderer for the provision of the required equipment through the purchase of sterile single use consumables.

title-proc.eng: Request for Tender for the provision of a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in maths among children and young people in Ireland with a particular focus on girls and young women

eng: The Department is seeking research services from a suitably qualified contractor(s) to conduct a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in mathematics among children and young people in Ireland, with a particular focus on girls and young women. For the purposes of this review, the terms children and young people and girls and young women refer to learners from the early learning and care (ELC) sector through primary and post-primary education. The review should therefore consider evidence relating to confidence in mathematics and numeracy, including learners' self-belief, mathematical self-efficacy, attitudes towards mathematics, and willingness to engage with mathematical learning across the continuum of educational provision, including key developmental and educational transition points.
Department of Education and Youth

title-proc.eng: New Pavilion, Refurbished Bath House and Public Realm located between the Cliff Road, The Hollows Carpark, Enniscrone Beach, the Cliff Bath House and old Slipway, Enniscrone, Co. Sligo

eng: Development consisting of the demolition of base of the former pavilion above the Hollows Car Park, the existing external stairways, ramps and walkways between the existing Pavilion and the Cliff Bath House along with general associated external works. The construction of a new two-story Community Pavilion comprising Community Use at ground floor and Cafe at first floor level and Viewing Areas at roof Level; circulation by way of ramps, stairs and lift connecting the Hollows car park to ground floor, first floor, roof level up to the Cliff Road with public accessible open deck at roof level and associated alterations to the external adjacent areas including a landscaped area along the Hollows car park. The construction of new Outdoor Performance Area in the Grassy Area north of the Cliff Bathhouse; the removal of the existing Gathering Space area on the Upper Promenade and its replacement with a new sheltered hedged landscaped Gathering Space. The refurbishment, repair, internal alterations and general conservation works to the existing Cliff Bath House, a Protected Structure. The alterations to include the installation of sauna cabins, the restoration of one seaweed bath room and associated facilities; external alterations to include new windows, doors, pin head roof lights and access deck connecting with the new deck walkway. New maritime landscaping is proposed to the Cliff Public Realm. The removal of a section of wall along the Cliff Road to facilitate the construction of a new widened Boardwalk on the Cliff Road leading to a new Viewing Area with a new Covered Colonnade below and a new Accessible Ramp leading down from the street to the Upper Promenade; the construction of a new Accessible ramp leading from the Upper Promenade to the proposed new Community Pavilion; the construction of a new Diagonal ramp leading from the Upper Promenade to the Lower Promenade to include the removal of a section of the Lower Promenade retaining wall; the installation of 5 no. Covered Shelters along the Lower Promenade and the existing Stepped Ramp at the northern end; the installation of a new Accessible Walkway from the north end of the Lower Promenade adjacent to the Cliff Bank behind the Clift Bath House leading to the Old Slipway with a link to the Cliff Bath House; a new retaining wall with replacement steps leading back up the grassy area at the Cliff Road; the construction of New Accessible Toilets behind the existing stone Retaining Wall opposite the Cliff Bath House. The provision of new foul and surface water drainage systems, water services, mechanical and electrical services, CCTV including discreet low impact external lighting along principal walkways and promenades
Sligo County Council

description-proc.eng: Development consisting of the demolition of base of the former pavilion above the Hollows Car Park, the existing external stairways, ramps and walkways between the existing Pavilion and the Cliff Bath House along with general associated external works. The construction of a new two-story Community Pavilion comprising Community Use at ground floor and Cafe at first floor level and Viewing Areas at roof Level; circulation by way of ramps, stairs and lift connecting the Hollows car park to ground floor, first floor, roof level up to the Cliff Road with public accessible open deck at roof level and associated alterations to the external adjacent areas including a landscaped area along the Hollows car park. The construction of new Outdoor Performance Area in the Grassy Area north of the Cliff Bathhouse; the removal of the existing Gathering Space area on the Upper Promenade and its replacement with a new sheltered hedged landscaped Gathering Space. The refurbishment, repair, internal alterations and general conservation works to the existing Cliff Bath House, a Protected Structure. The alterations to include the installation of sauna cabins, the restoration of one seaweed bath room and associated facilities; external alterations to include new windows, doors, pin head roof lights and access deck connecting with the new deck walkway. New maritime landscaping is proposed to the Cliff Public Realm. The removal of a section of wall along the Cliff Road to facilitate the construction of a new widened Boardwalk on the Cliff Road leading to a new Viewing Area with a new Covered Colonnade below and a new Accessible Ramp leading down from the street to the Upper Promenade; the construction of a new Accessible ramp leading from the Upper Promenade to the proposed new Community Pavilion; the construction of a new Diagonal ramp leading from the Upper Promenade to the Lower Promenade to include the removal of a section of the Lower Promenade retaining wall; the installation of 5 no. Covered Shelters along the Lower Promenade and the existing Stepped Ramp at the northern end; the installation of a new Accessible Walkway from the north end of the Lower Promenade adjacent to the Cliff Bank behind the Clift Bath House leading to the Old Slipway with a link to the Cliff Bath House; a new retaining wall with replacement steps leading back up the grassy area at the Cliff Road; the construction of New Accessible Toilets behind the existing stone Retaining Wall opposite the Cliff Bath House. The provision of new foul and surface water drainage systems, water services, mechanical and electrical services, CCTV including discreet low impact external lighting along principal walkways and promenades

title-proc.eng: Request for Tenders for the Provision of Consultancy Services to Revenue (National VRT Service) in respect of the Valuation of Motor Vehicles and other Related Services

eng: Provision of Consultancy Services to Revenue (National VRT Service) in respect of the Valuation of Motor Vehicles and other Related Services. The successful Tenderer will be required to provide opinions of the Open Market Selling Price (OMSP) of motor vehicles (i.e. the price, inclusive of all taxes and duties, which motor vehicles might reasonably be expected to fetch on a first arm’s length sale thereof in this State by retail) and technical advice in respect of motor vehicles. The successful tenderer will be expected to have; Significant expertise in the valuation of motor vehicles in Ireland. Expertise in the valuation of used vehicles imported from the UK, Japan and other jurisdictions is particularly important. Specialist expertise in the full spectrum of electric, hybrid and electric hybrid vehicles. The successful Tenderer will undertake the physical examination of vehicle(s), at the request of Revenue.
Office of the Revenue Commissioners_366

title-proc.eng: Single Party Framework Consultancy for the Development of a Parking Strategy for Limerick

eng: Limerick City Centre is undergoing a holistic change in the way that it manages its commuter traffic. The way in which commuters can use the road network within the city centre is being changed with the introduction of viable alternatives to the traditional car centric philosophies of the past. Enhancements through the introduction of Active travel infrastructure and future plans with respect to LSMATs and Bus connects projects will provide commuters with real viable alternatives when travelling to and from the City centre. The Mayoral program, supported by the Draft Limerick City Centre Transport Plan has the potential to enact further change in the way the city is viewed from a commuter perspective. Limerick City and County Council are aware that the proposed changes will create a number of opportunities and challenges for commuters, with one such challenge being the change to existing on street parking. It is the intention of this appointment to develop a parking strategy that will provide Limerick City and County Council a clear philosophy in the management of the existing and projected on street parking in the short, medium and long term as the projects outlined above come to fruition.
Limerick City and County Council_103432

Within this context, the CDDP will be guided by best international practice in conservation design and interpretation.

title-proc.eng: Establishment of a multi-party Integrated Design Team Framework

eng: Provision of a multi-party Integrated Design Team Framework Trinity College Dublin (“Trinity” / “TCD”) Capital Programmes Office has a need to establish an Integrated Design Team (“IDT”) Framework Panel (the “Framework” / “Panel”) to support the organisation’s capital works programme. The Framework adopts a multi-disciplinary model in which one Principal Service Provider (“PSP”) shall be nominated as Lead Consultant for each Call-Off, assuming responsibility for coordination and delivery of the Integrated Design Team. The Framework will provide a compliant, efficient, and high quality mechanism for appointing multi-disciplinary design teams across multiple projects over a defined period. It will ensure consistency of design quality, value for money, and adherence to procurement regulations. The Framework shall operate within the scope of the Capital Works Management Frameworks (“CWMF”) and National and EU procurement regulations.
Trinity College Dublin the University of Dublin_336

description-proc.eng: Provision of a multi-party Integrated Design Team Framework Trinity College Dublin (“Trinity” / “TCD”) Capital Programmes Office has a need to establish an Integrated Design Team (“IDT”) Framework Panel (the “Framework” / “Panel”) to support the organisation’s capital works programme. The Framework adopts a multi-disciplinary model in which one Principal Service Provider (“PSP”) shall be nominated as Lead Consultant for each Call-Off, assuming responsibility for coordination and delivery of the Integrated Design Team. The Framework will provide a compliant, efficient, and high quality mechanism for appointing multi-disciplinary design teams across multiple projects over a defined period. It will ensure consistency of design quality, value for money, and adherence to procurement regulations. The Framework shall operate within the scope of the Capital Works Management Frameworks (“CWMF”) and National and EU procurement regulations.

title-proc.eng: Shesknan Bridge Works

eng: The project involves the replacement/rehabilitation of a single-span road bridge in poor structural condition and has partially collapsed. Works will focus on the replacement of bridge deck and parapet walls, abutment and wingwall re-pointing, vegetation clearance, and associated ancillary works. Shesknan Bridge is a single-span masonry arch bridge of approximately 6m span, supporting a local road crossing over a natural watercourse. The bridge consists of a masonry arch barrel, stone sidewalls and parapets, with a relatively shallow depth of fill material supporting the road surface above. The recommended solution for the bridge is full replacement. This addresses advanced deterioration including reinforcement corrosion, section loss and spalling, which render repair-only strategies uneconomical and short-lived. Additional works are anticipated to include the following:  Site mobilisation and establishment.  Temporary works and access provision.  Demolition of defective components.  Parapet, abutment and wingwall works.  Vegetation clearance and habitat measures.  Road reinstatement, surfacing and safety barrier installation.  Final inspection and handover.
Leitrim County Council_2136

title-proc.eng: Supply and Delivery of an Agricultural Tractor to the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine

eng: The Department Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) requires an agricultural tractor for use at Killybegs Fishery Harbour Centre (FHC), Killybegs, Co. Donegal. The principle function of the tractor shall be to tow vessels to and from dry dock bays in the Department shipyard. Vessels up to 600 tonnes are removed from the water on cradle trains using a vertical syncrolift facility. The tractor would be attached to the cradle train at ground level in order to tow the vessels into the dry dock bay or into the boat repair building.The successful tenderer shall provide as part of the contract price a comprehensive Warranty and Service/Maintenance Package for the tractor for the first 6000 hours or for a period of five (5) years commencing on the date of delivery of the vehicle-whichever comes first.
Department of Agriculture Food and the Marine

title-proc.eng: Specialist Consultancy Providers for Traditional Design Services and Technical Advisory Services Framework

eng: Framework for specialist consultancy and technical advisory services supporting Respond's housing development programme across Ireland. The Contracting Authority intends to establish a multi-disciplinary Framework for Specialist Consultancy Providers and Technical Advisory Services to support Respond Housing Association in the delivery of housing development projects throughout Ireland. The Framework will provide specialist consultancy services for both Traditional Design projects, where Respond acts as Developer/Employer, and Developer Led projects, where Respond has entered into a Development Agreement or similar arrangement with a third-party developer. The Framework will support Respond in the design, statutory approvals, procurement, monitoring, technical advisory and delivery of housing developments, including social, affordable and cost rental accommodation.

title-proc.eng: T.083.2026 Request for Tenders to establish a Single-Supplier Framework for the provision of Temporary CCTV and related Services for Special Events as a Managed Service, for An Garda Síochána

eng: In summary, the services requested comprise of the provision of temporary CCTV and related Services for outdoor Special Events and VIP Visits as a Managed Service. The Contracting Authority will require the successful Tenderer to have the ability to provide services they are tendering for within short notice i.e. 48 hours. The Contracting Authority will establish a single-supplier framework for the provision of the following services individually or in combination to support policing operations during special events (including VIP visits): • The provision of CCTV Services (including the provision, installation and maintenance of cameras, video links, and a video evidence management solution); • The provision of a communications vehicle (or vehicles) with equipment necessary to provide control room functionality and to support incident management); • The provision of large (outdoor) video displays; and, • The provision of a public announcement (“PA”) system (or systems). The successful Tenderer will be responsible for sourcing and providing the equipment listed above along with the provision of ancillary services and equipment necessary to provide the equipment above as a managed service.
An Garda Síochána_1192

title-proc.eng: Upgrade works to the existing Cootehill Enterprise Centre, including thermal performance improvements and environmental upgrades to the external building envelope andfaçade systems.

eng: Upgrade works to the existing Cootehill Enterprise Centre, comprising thermal performance improvements and environmental upgrades to the external building envelope and façade systems. The works are divided into five separate options, each of which shall be individually priced by the Contractor and included within the Form of Tender. The five option prices shall also be combined to provide an overall tender sum. The options comprise: Option 1 – Non-Insulated Façade Upgrade: Upgrade and refurbishment of the existing external façade without the provision of additional thermal insulation, including new building signage. Option 2 – Insulated Façade Upgrade: Upgrade of the existing external façade incorporating additional thermal insulation to improve the thermal performance of the building envelope, including new building signage. Option 3 – Window and Door Replacement: Removal and replacement of the existing external windows and doors with new thermally efficient units, complete with all associated making good, flashings, sealants and finishes. Option 4 – Photovoltaic Panels: Provision and installation of a new photovoltaic (PV) panel system, including all associated supports, electrical connections, controls and ancillary works. Option 5 – Internal Wall Insulation: Provision of internal wall insulation to the identified existing external wall constructions, including all associated linings, finishes, junction treatments and making good. Tenderers shall allow for all labour, materials, plant, access, temporary works, coordination and ancillary works necessary to provide a complete installation for each option.
Cavan County Enterprise Fund

title-proc.eng: Munster Technological University (MTU) High Performance Indoor Athletics Centre (HPAC) at Bishopstown Campus, Cork.

eng: This tender relates to the Construction of a part single / part three storey High Performance Indoor Athletics Training Centre (HPAC) with associated sports laboratories, classrooms, studios and plant (approx. area 5250sqm), along with an external roof terrace, and associated landscaping, site and services works. The new facility is to be located to the south of the existing running track within the main MTU Bishopstown campus located at Rossa Avenue, Bishopstown, Cork and will be connected to the existing MTU Arena at 1st and 2nd Floor levels. Full details are in the tender documentation attached to this Contract Notice.
Munster Technological University.

title-proc.eng: Single Supplier Party Framework for the Provision of Welding Equipment to Waterford and Wexford Education and Training Board

eng: This public procurement competition relates to the establishment of a Single Supplier Party Framework for the Provision of Welding Equipment to Waterford and Wexford Education and Training Board primarily in the WWETB Training Centres and Wexford College of Further Education. WWETB run Apprenticeship Training Programmes under Phase 2 of the Apprentice Training Programmes. The tender is divided into 3 Lots. Tenderers may submit proposals for one or more lots and must be clear on which lots they are tendering for in their response. The minimum contract awarded will be one Lot. The quantities may also be varied depending on the funding available. Tenderers may tender for one or several lots. The three lots are as follows: Lot 1 AC/ DC TIG/MMA Water Cooled Welding Machines (for both Welding and Plumbing departments) Lot 2 MIG/MAGS Welding Machines Lot 3 Water Cooled Multi Process Welding machines

title-proc.eng: Legacy marine data and rights to publish legacy marine data to include all of Ireland 2026

eng: The next phase of the State’s multi-phase approach to offshore wind delivery has seen a move to a plan-led model that will ensure ORE development and deployment is managed in a planned, strategic, and sustainable way, and enable a balanced equilibrium between achieving ORE objectives, while maintaining environmental protection, the economic well-being of local communities, and consideration of other activities taking place in our shared marine space. In turn, this will provide greater certainty for all maritime users as to where development will be situated. An important step in advancing Phase Two will be the use of forward spatial planning, and specifically the requirement to establish Offshore Renewable Energy (ORE) Designated Areas that will take place according to legislative provisions for Designated Maritime Area Plans (DMAPs) within the Maritime Area Planning (MAP) Act, 2021. This forward spatial planning will take an ecosystem-based approach, in line with EU and national policy, and will inter alia help to guide future investment and decision-making. The National DMAP will provide a spatial planning policy framework for offshore renewable energy deployment around Ireland’s coastline. The development and implementation of the National DMAP is currently underway. It will aim to designate sufficient maritime area to deliver Ireland’s ambition of having 20 GW of offshore renewable energy by 2040. Commencing with the South Coast DMAP, the State is undertaking comprehensive surveying activities through our partners in the Marine Institute (MI) and Geological Survey Ireland (GSI) or private surveyors as required to facilitate potential future offshore renewable energy development. This is taking place through a comprehensive programme of survey activity within the geographical area of each DMAP proposed and/or marine areas identified for offshore wind development within the future DMAPs, and/or marine areas identified for offshore wind development within the final DMAPs approved by the Oireachtas. In addition to the above anticipated programme of survey work, DCEE is seeking to supplement our own existing marine data with existing, high-quality, and unprocessed datasets which have been collected in recent years by private industry. description-proc.eng: The next phase of the State’s multi-phase approach to offshore wind delivery has seen a move to a plan-led model that will ensure ORE development and deployment is managed in a planned, strategic, and sustainable way, and enable a balanced equilibrium between achieving ORE objectives, while maintaining environmental protection, the economic well-being of local communities, and consideration of other activities taking place in our shared marine space. In turn, this will provide greater certainty for all maritime users as to where development will be situated. An important step in advancing Phase Two will be the use of forward spatial planning, and specifically the requirement to establish Offshore Renewable Energy (ORE) Designated Areas that will take place according to legislative provisions for Designated Maritime Area Plans (DMAPs) within the Maritime Area Planning (MAP) Act, 2021. This forward spatial planning will take an ecosystem-based approach, in line with EU and national policy, and will inter alia help to guide future investment and decision-making. The National DMAP will provide a spatial planning policy framework for offshore renewable energy deployment around Ireland’s coastline. The development and implementation of the National DMAP is currently underway. It will aim to designate sufficient maritime area to deliver Ireland’s ambition of having 20 GW of offshore renewable energy by 2040. Commencing with the South Coast DMAP, the State is undertaking comprehensive surveying activities through our partners in the Marine Institute (MI) and Geological Survey Ireland (GSI) or private surveyors as required to facilitate potential future offshore renewable energy development. This is taking place through a comprehensive programme of survey activity within the geographical area of each DMAP proposed and/or marine areas identified for offshore wind development within the future DMAPs, and/or marine areas identified for offshore wind development within the final DMAPs approved by the Oireachtas. In addition to the above anticipated programme of survey work, DCEE is seeking to supplement our own existing marine data with existing, high-quality, and unprocessed datasets which have been collected in recent years by private industry. This framework will focus on an all of Ireland approach (Irish Sea, Celtic Sea and Atlantic Ocean) and to potentially focus on other future DMAP areas as required. title-proc.eng: Dublin City Council Contract for Architect Led Integrated Design Team for the Installation of a Pontoon at Islandbridge

eng: The stretch of the River Liffey near Islandbridge, is home to over 13 Rowing Clubs – one of which belongs to Dublin City Council. In order to link the eastern length of the Liffey from Islandbridge, the Community, Culture and Local Area Services Department of Dublin City Council has obtained planning permission for an access walkway and pontoon to be constructed on one of the small islands east of the weir. This will allow rowers starting at Islandbridge to have access down to Ringsend and vice versa safely. The project comprises a pontoon with associated walkways to facilitate access to the river for rowing boats and kayaks. The project will provide for a platform that would minimize damage to bankside vegetation when launching and retrieving boats and allow a safe platform for kayakers and boaters to embark and disembark. The Islandbridge location has extensive heritage and ecology. In keeping with this, minimal deviation from the existing design and methodology is required to comply with planning regulations. The works proposed plan to combine the following elements: a) A floating pontoon system within the River Liffey anchored to the existing island shore. b) A new stone and concrete platform built out from the riverbank and connected to the pontoon by a new gangway. c) The removal of vegetation on approach to the pontoon and installation of a new access walkway from the south upper River Liffey at the weir to the new pontoon located north on the lower River Liffey. d) The temporary removal, refurbishment and reinstatement of an existing steel footbridge located on the island. e) The removal of poor existing vegetation, pruning of existing healthy trees and the replanting of 25 new high-quality trees and growing shrubs all native to Ireland. f) Temporary regrading of land during site works for access onto the island. . Please note that this project is subject to funding. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID xxxxxxx – Input when notice created.
Dublin City Council

title-proc.eng: Single Party Framework Agreement for the Provision of Energy Efficient Design Services

eng: The Energy Efficient Design (EED) process is intended to ensure that the Contracting Authority’s capital projects are conducted in accordance with objective and methodical protocols and procedures. The overall EED process comprises organisational measures, processes, guiding principles and control mechanisms to be implemented during the design of projects, with the targets of (i) reducing the lifecycle energy consumption and GHG emissions of the building when in use and (ii) achieving a building that is Carbon Zero Ready (i.e., a building that will be carbon zero when the electrical grid decarbonises). In accordance with national and sectoral guidance, the EED process shall be applied to all projects with a value greater than €1,000,000. The purpose of this competition is to appoint a suitably-qualified and experienced EED Facilitator who will draft and submit key EED reports in accordance with this Specification of Requirements document. Such reports will serve to measure progress of the EED process as applied to each capital project and effectively communicate the results of the EED process to Contracting Authority project stakeholders.

title-proc.eng: Multi-Party Framework Agreement for the Provision of a Non-Operative Treatment Pathway for Low Complexity Spinal Patients

eng: The Contracting Authority intends to establish a framework agreement with suitably-qualified and experienced medical service providers to deliver end-to-end outpatient assessment, diagnostic and non-operative treatment pathways for a cohort of approximately 1,200 patients. These patients are currently on a neurosurgical waiting list, rather than an orthopaedic list; however, the Contracting Authority will accept tender submissions involving orthopaedic spinal surgeon review. For tenderers’ information, a low-complexity spine patient is defined as an individual with a straightforward, one or two level or localised spinal condition that requires standard surgical or medical management with minimal technical difficulty and lower physiological risk. Under the framework agreement, the successful tenderers will assume responsibility for patients from the first specialist outpatient assessment to the patient’s discharge or until a determination has been made that surgical intervention is clinically indicated. It is a mandatory condition for the operation of this framework agreement that appointed framework operators are eligible to deliver low-complexity spine procedures under the relevant National Surgical Services Framework.
Beaumont Hospital_403

title-proc.eng: 26-007F National Multi-Supplier Framework for the Provision of Laboratory Services

eng: "Uisce Eireann require potable water laboratory testing services for the following sampling categories: • PLANNED (Drinking Water Directive – Schedule 1 & Schedule 2); • UNPLANNED (Investigative; Short term requests e.g. EPA) • EMERGENCY. For each of the categories above, Uisce Eireann may require a combination of Sampling and Testing services (i.e. taking the sample, transport to the supplier’s laboratory, analysis and reporting), a Collection and Testing service (i.e. collection of sample(s) from a designated collection point(s), transport to the supplier’s laboratory, analysis and reporting) and Testing Only (receipt of samples delivered to the suppliers laboratory analysis and reporting). With regards to the PLANNED, UNPLANNED, and EMERGENCY categories, Uisce Eireann may also require sampling and/or testing of raw water (i.e. ground water or surface water), and In-Process Water (i.e. samples taken from locations within the treatment process). Additional Services may be procured through the course of the framework to facilitate various investigative activities including but not limited to the following areas of work:- • Process Optimisation • Process Proving / Commissioning These additional services may be PLANNED or UNPLANNED in nature."

"Uisce Eireann require wastewater laboratory testing services for the following sampling categories: • PLANNED (Wastewater Regulatory Sampling Plans ); • UNPLANNED (Investigative; Short term requests e.g. EPA) • EMERGENCY. For each of the categories above, Uisce Eireann may require a combination of Sampling and Testing services (i.e. taking the sample, transport to the supplier’s laboratory, analysis and reporting), a Collection and Testing service (i.e. collection of sample(s) from a designated collection point(s), transport to the supplier’s laboratory, analysis and reporting) and Testing Only (receipt of samples delivered to the suppliers laboratory analysis and reporting). The applicant should also have the capability to undertake analysis of samples from saline waters. With regards to the PLANNED, UNPLANNED, and EMERGENCY categories, Uisce Eireann may also require sampling and/or testing of In-Process Wastewater (i.e. samples taken from locations within the treatment process). Additional Services may be procured through the course of the framework to facilitate various investigative activities including but not limited to the following areas of work:- • Process Optimisation • Process Proving / Commissioning • Flow and Load Surveys • Sludge Testing These additional services may be PLANNED or UNPLANNED in nature."

Uisce Eireann require the provision of Drinking Water & Wastewater contingency and surge laboratory testing services to maintain continuity during equipment failure, accreditation loss, or capacity constraints.
Uisce Éireann

description-proc.eng: Uisce Eireann is seeking to establish a high-quality sampling and or analysis service to achieve efficiencies in all commercial laboratory contractual arrangements, to meet regulatory requirements, and to protect public health. These services will be sub-divided into Three (3) Lots described below as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Applicants may apply for one, some or all Lots. For Lots 1, 2 and 3 the successful tenderers may be allocated as preferred supplier for a Geographical Region or Regions on the basis of their tenders and there may be a limit on the number of Regions for which a single supplier achieves preferred supplier status. It is anticipated that Uisce Eireann will enter into separate framework agreements for each of the following Lots: Lot 1 - Potable Water Laboratory Testing Services. Uisce Eireann require potable water laboratory testing services for the following sampling categories: • PLANNED (Drinking Water Directive – Schedule 1 and Schedule 2) • UNPLANNED (Investigative; Short term requests e.g. EPA) • EMERGENCY. For each of the categories above, Uisce Eireann may require a combination of Sampling and Testing services (i.e. taking the sample, transport to the supplier’s laboratory, analysis and reporting), a Collection and Testing service (i.e. collection of sample(s) from a designated collection point(s), transport to the supplier’s laboratory, analysis and reporting) and Testing Only (receipt of samples delivered to the suppliers laboratory analysis and reporting). With regards to the PLANNED, UNPLANNED, and EMERGENCY categories, Uisce Eireann may also require sampling and/or testing of raw water (i.e. ground water or surface water), and In-Process Water (i.e. samples taken from locations within the treatment process). Additional Services may be procured through the course of the framework to facilitate various investigative activities including but not limited to the following areas of work:- • Process Optimisation • Process Proving / Commissioning These additional services may be PLANNED or UNPLANNED in nature. Lot 2: Provision of Wastewater Laboratory Testing Services. Uisce Eireann require wastewater laboratory testing services for the following sampling categories: • PLANNED (Wastewater Regulatory Sampling Plans ) • UNPLANNED (Investigative; Short term requests e.g. EPA) • EMERGENCY. For each of the categories above, Uisce Eireann may require a combination of Sampling and Testing services (i.e. taking the sample, transport to the supplier’s laboratory, analysis and reporting), a Collection and Testing service (i.e. collection of sample(s) from a designated collection point(s), transport to the supplier’s laboratory, analysis and reporting) and Testing Only (receipt of samples delivered to the suppliers laboratory analysis and reporting). The applicant should also have the capability to undertake analysis of samples from saline waters. With regards to the PLANNED, UNPLANNED, and EMERGENCY categories, Uisce Eireann may also require sampling and/or testing of In-Process Wastewater (i.e. samples taken from locations within the treatment process). Additional Services may be procured through the course of the framework to facilitate various investigative activities including but not limited to the following areas of work:- • Process Optimisation • Process Proving / Commissioning • Flow and Load Surveys • Sludge Testing These additional services may be PLANNED or UNPLANNED in nature. Lot 3: Provision of Contingency outsourcing of Laboratory Testing Services. Uisce Eireann require the provision of Drinking Water and Wastewater contingency and surge laboratory testing services to maintain continuity during equipment failure, accreditation loss, or capacity constraints.

title-proc.eng: Supply and delivery of HVO-ready Vehicles for Inland Fisheries Ireland in two Lots

Tenderers are required to provide details of manufacturer approvals for the use of paraffinic fuel including Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO). There are two Lots - Category M1 passenger vehicles with a minimum 5 (five) seater occupancy and Category N1 2 (two) seater commercial vehicles.

title-proc.eng: OPERATIONAL LEASE OF ONE WHEELCHAIR-ACCESSIBLE VAN AND ONE CAR

eng: Depaul Ireland invites suitably qualified and experienced vehicle leasing providers to submit tenders for the operational lease of one wheelchair-accessible van (Lot 1) and one car (Lot 2) for a period of 36 months, with full maintenance included. Depaul Ireland is a charity working with individuals and families experiencing homelessness and those at risk of homelessness. Its services include emergency accommodation, supported housing, Housing First, health and wellbeing services, community-based support and administrative functions. description-proc.eng: This tender competition is for the delivery of a health coaching-aligned and physical activity coaching programme as part of a multi-disciplinary obesity care programme to 5000 patients living in the Derry GP Federation area. PEACETIME is a cross-border research project and will include work in Donegal, but respondents to this tender competition are bidding for delivery of work in the Derry GP Federation area only. This tender competition is being managed by the Derry GP Federation, who are a partner in the PEACETIME project. A contract between the Derry GP Federation and the tenderer(s) will be finalised ahead of formal go ahead for the delivery of the project. Service Providers are requested to submit a tender, only if they are confident that they have the requisite experience and expertise as outlined in the project documentation, commencing as soon as is practicable after award of contract. The provider(s) should be operationally ready to deliver the intervention in the Autumn of 2026.

title-proc.eng: EST_MW - Maternity Emergency and Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit - University Maternity Hospital Limerick

eng: The development is located on the existing site of the Maternity Hospital at UMHL delivering acute hospital services and will consist of a new rapid build facility with a gross internal floor area of circa. 863m2. The proposed development includes two floors (ground, first), plus a rooftop plantroom area of circa. 150m2. The development also consists of the refurbishment of the existing Main Entrance and Medical Emergency Unit (area circa. 263m2). The development will provide for the refurbishment of the main hospital reception, the expansion and refurbishment of the existing Maternity Emergency Unit, a new extension providing a diagnostic scanning suite, a 3 bed assessment unit on the ground floor, a 4 bed labour induction unit, a 2 room Intensive Care suite and a Procedure room on the first floor along with general support and staff facilities. The development also includes a new main entrance draught lobby and entrance canopy along with an upgraded Main Entrance forecourt with associated landscape works. It is proposed to construct a new car park to the south east of the site for car parking displaced by the new development and associated landscape works.
Health Service Executive (HSE)

title-proc.eng: Killeen and Feenune Bridge Barrier Mitigation Project

eng: Inland Fisheries Ireland is seeking to procure multidisciplinary consultancy services to assist with the delivery of two Barrier Mitigation Projects: Killeen Bridge and Feenune Bridge near Louisburgh in Co. Mayo, through the completion of Phases 1 to 3. The appointed Consultant will undertake all necessary engineering, environmental and planning services required to progress the project through feasibility, option selection, and statutory consent stages in accordance with the Planning and Development Acts 2000–2023, the Capital Works Management Framework, and Infrastructure Guidelines 2023. The Barrier Mitigation Projects aim to mitigate the impacts of the identified barriers on fish passage and restore more natural river processes along the associated rivers. The commission forms a specific action under Ireland’s Water Action Plan 2024 and supports implementation of the National Barrier Mitigation Programme to deliver improved ecological status under the EU Water Framework Directive. The Consultant will act as the Designer, Project Supervisor Design Process during Phases 1 to 3 of the project and carry out all related necessary duties.
Inland Fisheries Ireland

title-proc.eng: Request for Tenders dated 01/10/2026 for the provision of maintenance services for Met Eireann’s environmental monitoring instrumentation and related infrastructure at Bray Head, Valentia Island

eng: Met Éireann has committed significant resources to its programmes that support Ireland’s Atmospheric Composition and Climate Change (AC3) network and national research and monitoring infrastructure. These resources include buildings, equipment and staff that espouse international coordinated programmes which include; the Global Atmosphere Watch (GAW) Programme, the “European Monitoring and Evaluation Programme” (EMEP), Integrated Carbon Observation System (ICOS) and GHG emissions and Short Lived Climate Forcers (SLCF) monitoring. These programmes have developed incrementally and have adhered to best practice from pan-European and global monitoring programmes. Details of some of these programmes are included in Appendix 1 of the RFT. Met Éireann has a dedicated facility at Bray Head on Valentia Island, which is shortly to be verified as an ICOS Class 2 site, which hosts monitoring equipment for monitoring atmospheric gases and aerosols. The data can also be used for emissions verification, through an inverse modelling process, of greenhouse gases and pollutants and facilitate the calculation of Ireland’s emissions and Ireland’s greenhouse gas inventories and projections. The tender relates to the provision of support services, data validation, calibration and maintenance for some of the instrumentation and associated data streams.
Met Eireann

title-proc.eng: 9843 Design and Build Capacity Enhancement Works at Connolly Station

eng: This is a call for competition by Iarnród Éireann for the procurement of an experienced Design and Build Contractor to complete the design and deliver capacity enhancement and transformation works at Connolly Station. The project will create a new entrance from Preston Street and a passenger concourse within the historic Victorian undercroft, together with new lifts, escalators and staircases providing improved access to Platforms 5, 6 and 7. The works will also include additional emergency escape routes, public-realm improvements, retail, operational and back-of-house spaces, heritage refurbishment, structural alterations and the installation or modification of station and railway systems. The successful Contractor will be required to review and develop the reference design through detailed design to Approved for Construction status and subsequently construct, test and commission the works. The Contractor will also be responsible for providing complete as-built and handover information. The project will be delivered within a constrained, live operational railway environment. The Contractor will be required to manage passenger circulation, railway access, construction phasing, safety assurance, stakeholder engagement, heritage requirements and interfaces with other DART+ contracts. The appointed Contractor will undertake the role of Project Supervisor for the Construction Stage. The form of contract is currently anticipated to be the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract, Option C, target contract with activity schedule. This procurement is a reissue of an earlier competition published in May 2025 under procedure identifier e342e2b9-7827-4a53-81b6-5178881e0fa0 and eTenders reference ID 5643930, which was subsequently discontinued without the award of a contract.
Iarnród Eireann-Irish Rail

title-proc.eng: T.083.2026 Request for Tenders to establish a Single-Supplier Framework for the provision of Temporary CCTV and related Services for Special Events as a Managed Service, for An Garda Síochána

eng: In summary, the services requested comprise of the provision of temporary CCTV and related Services for outdoor Special Events and VIP Visits as a Managed Service. The Contracting Authority will require the successful Tenderer to have the ability to provide services they are tendering for within short notice i.e. 48 hours. The Contracting Authority will establish a single-supplier framework for the provision of the following services individually or in combination to support policing operations during special events (including VIP visits): • The provision of CCTV Services (including the provision, installation and maintenance of cameras, video links, and a video evidence management solution); • The provision of a communications vehicle (or vehicles) with equipment necessary to provide control room functionality and to support incident management); • The provision of large (outdoor) video displays; and, • The provision of a public announcement (“PA”) system (or systems). The successful Tenderer will be responsible for sourcing and providing the equipment listed above along with the provision of ancillary services and equipment necessary to provide the equipment above as a managed service.
An Garda Síochána_1192

title-proc.eng: Dublin City Council Contract for Works Contractor for Public Realm and Building Works at Library Square Ringsend

eng: Public Realm and road works over approx. 0.5ha and building construction and refurbishment works over approximately 600sqm The project involves the realignment of Irishtown Road and the reconstruction and repaving of Library Square and Fitzwilliam Street with significant public realm (including high quality stone paving), landscaping and SUDs improvements, along with miscellaneous utility realignment and improvement works. The project also includes the refurbishment and extension of Ringsend Library. The Contractor will be responsible for all construction works as well as the management of traffic and safety on site.. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie. Please note that this project is subject to funding. The maximum number of candidates to be selected to tender is 8.
Dublin City Council

title-proc.eng: Establishment of a Multi-Party Framework Agreement for Fitness to Practise Legal Services

eng: NMBI wishes to establish a Multi-Party Framework Agreement for Fitness to Practise Legal Services. The primary role of the legal firm(s) engaged under this procurement process will be to prepare and present cases on behalf of the CEO with respect to registrants who have been referred to inquiry. The responsibilities will also include liaison and collaboration with all participants in the inquiry process (complainants, factual and expert witnesses, registrants, their legal counsel and the Contracting Authority staff). The legal firm will oversee and guide the progression of an inquiry to a timely conclusion. Following an inquiry where a sanction is recommended and subsequently imposed on a registrant by the Board, the legal firm will be responsible for seeking High Court Confirmation of sanction where required in accordance with the Nurses and Midwives Act 2011. Further detail as to required services is set out in three phases – before, during and after an inquiry when the Board decides to impose a sanction which requires High Court confirmation in accordance with the Nurses and Midwives Act 2011.
Bord Altranais agus Cnáimhseachais na hÉireann Nursing and Midwifery Board of Ireland

title-proc.eng: Consultancy Services to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case in relation to the provision of Irish-language based early-years (Naíonra) facilities in Dún Gar

eng: Naíonra Garbháin was established in 1981 as an early-immersion Irish-language based educational setting for pre-school children in Dún Garbhán and the surrounding areas. Dún Garbhán is a Baile Seirbhíse Gaeltachta (Gaeltacht Service Town). Naíonra Garbháin provides education and childcare services for people from the Gaeltacht who do not have access to housing in An Rinn or An Sean Phobal and who live in the surrounding area. Naíonra Garbháin is managed by a voluntary committee known as Croí na nÓg. As it is located immediately adjacent to the Irish-language based primary school, Scoil Gharbháin, progression from the Naíonra to the primary school is seamless and therefore the Naíonra is an important foundation and integral part of life on the Scoil Gharbháin campus. As the population of the town of Dún Garbháin, and in particular the area adjacent to the Naíonra, continues to grow, Croí na nÓg wishes to ensure that the facilities provided in the town of Dún Garbháin are sufficient to cater for the demand for Irish-language based education for pre-school children in the town. It also wishes to ensure that suitable facilities are available to cater for the demand for Irish-language based pre- and post-school services in the area. The latter is particularly important as a significant number of parents of primary school travel into Dún Garbháin on a daily basis for employment and are likely to avail of such services if they were available. Croí na nÓg have recently purchased lands immediately adjoining the Department of Education and Skills lands upon which Scoil Gharbháin is constructed and wish to ensure that the lands are utilised in the most efficient manner possible to meet the Irish-language based early education and pre/post school service demands of the area. Croí na nÓg wish to appoint a consultant to undertake a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case as envisaged in the Infrastructure Guidelines and the tender documents to improve the range of early-years educational and pre/post school services in the area.
Croí na nÓg

description-proc.eng: Naíonra Garbháin was established in 1981 as an early-immersion Irish-language based educational setting for pre-school children in Dún Garbhán and the surrounding areas. Dún Garbhán is a Baile Seirbhíse Gaeltachta (Gaeltacht Service Town). Naíonra Garbháin provides education and childcare services for people from the Gaeltacht who do not have access to housing in An Rinn or An Sean Phobal and who live in the surrounding area. Naíonra Garbháin is managed by a voluntary committee known as Croí na nÓg. As it is located immediately adjacent to the Irish-language based primary school, Scoil Gharbháin, progression from the Naíonra to the primary school is seamless and therefore the Naíonra is an important foundation and integral part of life on the Scoil Gharbháin campus. As the population of the town of Dún Garbháin, and in particular the area adjacent to the Naíonra, continues to grow, Croí na nÓg wishes to ensure that the facilities provided in the town of Dún Garbháin are sufficient to cater for the demand for Irish-language based education for pre-school children in the town. It also wishes to ensure that suitable facilities are available to cater for the demand for Irish-language based pre- and post-school services in the area. The latter is particularly important as a significant number of parents of primary school travel into Dún Garbháin on a daily basis for employment and are likely to avail of such services if they were available. Croí na nÓg have recently purchased lands immediately adjoining the Department of Education and Skills lands upon which Scoil Gharbháin is constructed and wish to ensure that the lands are utilised in the most efficient manner possible to meet the Irish-language based early education and pre/post school service demands of the area. Croí na nÓg wish to appoint a consultant to undertake a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case as envisaged in the Infrastructure Guidelines and the tender documents to improve the range of early-years educational and pre/post school services in the area.

title-proc.eng: Dublin City Council Single Party Framework Agreement for an Integrated Design Team for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project

eng: The Contracting Authority, Dublin City Council, intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a Integrated Design Team to deliver planning, engineering, environmental, stakeholder engagement and other specialist consultancy services for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project (CFDPRP). The Project is located along the Clontarf waterfront in Dublin and encompasses a highly sensitive coastal environment adjoining designated European sites, including Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA). The Project has been initiated to address existing and future coastal and surface water flood risks while delivering a coordinated programme of public realm enhancement, active travel improvements and environmental benefits. The scheme shall be developed through an integrated design approach that balances flood resilience, climate adaptation, biodiversity, heritage, placemaking, sustainable mobility, environmental protection and stakeholder aspirations. The initial call-off contract under the Framework will require the successful Applicant to undertake all services necessary to develop the Project from commencement through option identification, scheme development, environmental assessment, statutory consent processes and detailed design. This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 9181107. Please note that this project is subject to funding.
Dublin City Council

description-proc.eng: The Contracting Authority, Dublin City Council, intends to establish a Single Party Framework Agreement with a Integrated Design Team to deliver planning, engineering, environmental, stakeholder engagement and other specialist consultancy services for the Clontarf Flood Defence and Public Realm Project (CFDPRP). The Project is located along the Clontarf waterfront in Dublin and encompasses a highly sensitive coastal environment adjoining designated European sites, including Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA). The Project has been initiated to address existing and future coastal and surface water flood risks while delivering a coordinated programme of public realm enhancement, active travel improvements and environmental benefits. The scheme shall be developed through an integrated design approach that balances flood resilience, climate adaptation, biodiversity, heritage, placemaking, sustainable mobility, environmental protection and stakeholder aspirations. The initial call-off contract under the Framework will require the successful Applicant to undertake all services necessary to develop the Project from commencement through option identification, scheme development, environmental assessment, statutory consent processes and detailed design. This shall include the preparation of all technical studies, surveys, modelling, assessments, reports, designs and application documentation required to secure the necessary approvals and to progress the Project to a stage suitable for procurement and construction. The Framework Agreement may subsequently be utilised by the Contracting Authority to procure additional related services, including procurement support, construction-stage services, post-consent services and other specialist consultancy services associated with the delivery of the Project. The successful Applicant shall be required to develop a fully integrated and coordinated scheme that delivers flood protection, surface water management, active travel and public realm objectives within a single coherent design solution that is environmentally sensitive, climate resilient and appropriate to the strategic importance of the Clontarf waterfront. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID 9181107. Please note that this project is subject to funding.

title-proc.eng: Multi- Party Framework Agreement for HSE Design Team Services Framework 2024 - Framework 02 Acute Healthcare Capital Works - Project Value €1M to €15M excl. VAT for HSE NW

eng: MULTI-PARTY FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT FOR HSE DESIGN TEAM SERVICES FRAMEWORK 2024 – FRAMEWORK 02: ACUTE HEALTHCARE CAPITAL WORKS – PROJECT VALUE €1M -€15M EXCL. VAT. This framework will include the following design team disciplines (Lots): Lot 1: Architect(AR) as Principal Service Provider with the following Specialists domestic sub-consultants, or in-house specialisms: a. Planner (PL), b. Project Supervisor Design Process (PSDP), c. Fire Safety Consultant (FSC) and d. BIM Information Manager(BIM). Lot 2: Quantity Surveyor (QS), as Principal Service Provider. Lot 3: Building Services Engineer (M+E), as Principal Service Provider. Lot 4: Civil / Structural Engineer (C+S), as Principal Service Provider. Lot 5: Employer’s Representative (ER),as Principal Service Provider. Lot 6: Energy Efficient Design Facilitator (EEDF), as Principal Service Provider. Lot 7: Assigned Certifier (AC), as Principal Service Provider. The Health Services Executive (HSE) invites expressions of interest, under the Restricted Procedure, from suitably qualified services providers for the provision of design team services (including Specialist Skills Providers) per the above Lot listing for which it is proposed to establish a Multi-Party Framework Agreement for each Lot type to award call-off contracts for Acute Healthcare Capital Works – project value €1M-€15M excl. VAT within HSE North West Area Please note that the INITIAL project forming Framework 02 for this regional / sub¬regional office NW West Area will be: Proposed Microbiology Lab incorporating ancillary site works, plus enabling work to divert existing services at Sligo University Hospital. Please see SAQ document pack.

title-proc.eng: Green Capital Grant - Technical Assessments

eng: IDA Ireland supports eligible client sustainability investments through its Green Capital programme. As part of IDA Ireland’s investment approval process for Green Capital projects, an independent technical assessment is required to review the technical basis of each project and to validate or re-quantify its expected environmental impact. To date, technical assessments have been completed by a number of different assessors. As the volume and range of Green Capital investments increase, IDA Ireland requires a more consistent and scalable framework to support these technical reviews. IDA Ireland is seeking to appoint one service provider with the capability to manage and deliver all IDA Green Capital Technical Assessment services covered by this RFT. These will cover pre-investment technical assessments and post-investment Measurement and Verification (M and V) assessments.

eng: Bord Bia proposes to establish a framework agreement for the provision of Origin Green Mentorship Services, comprising the following service streams: • Provision of Generalist Mentorship Support, including structured one-to-one support to Origin Green members on programme requirements, reporting, and implementation. This support will focus on providing practical, step-by-step guidance to enable members, particularly SMEs, to understand and meet programme expectations. It will include assistance with assistance with understanding targets, materiality, and sustainability strategy development, as well as general sustainability advisory. • Provision of Subject Matter Expert Support, including technical advisory services across a range of sustainability areas, together with the design and delivery of in-depth Learning Labs that provide practical tools, frameworks, and implementation guidance.

description-proc.eng: Bord Bia proposes to establish a framework agreement for the provision of Origin Green Mentorship Services, comprising the following service streams: • Provision of Generalist Mentorship Support, including structured one-to-one support to Origin Green members on programme requirements, reporting, and implementation. This support will focus on providing practical, step-by-step guidance to enable members, particularly SMEs, to understand and meet programme expectations. title-proc.ita: FORNITURA DI HARDWARE PER IL POTENZIAMENTO DEL SISTEMA DI SUPERCALCOLO GALILEO 100 E RELATIVI SERVIZI CONNESSI

ita: CINECA Consorzio Interuniversitario in veste di stazione appaltante delegata da parte dell’Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale e dall’Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, intende procedere, in applicazione dell’art. 62, comma 14, d.lgs. 36/2023, all’acquisizione di un sistema che erogherà servizi di calcolo ad alte prestazioni e di virtualizzazione per le infrastrutture di ricerca e per la comunità di utenti CINECA, affiancando e complementando il sistema adacloud (https://adacloud.hpc.cineca.it/) e i sistemi HPC Tier0 e Tier1 già operativi. Progettualità cui si accede: • PNRR - Investimento 3.1 “Fondo per la realizzazione di un sistema integrato di infrastrutture di ricerca e innovazione” nell’ambito della Missione 4 Componente 2, in cui convergono i progetti “Terabit network for Research and Academic Big data in Italy” (CUP I53C21000370006) e “MEET – Monitoring Earth’s Evolution and Tectonics” (CUP D53C22001400005); • PNRR - Investimento 1.4 “Potenziamento strutture di ricerca e creazione di campioni nazionali di R&S su alcune Key Enabling Technologies”, nell’ambito della Missione 4 Componente 2, a cui accede il progetto “National Centre for HPC, Big Data and Quantum Computing”, relativo all’Area Tematica: “Simulazioni, calcolo e analisi dei dati ad alte prestazioni” (CUP D56G22000380006); • PNC - Iniziativa “Digital Driven Diagnostics, prognostics and therapeutics for sustainable Health care” identificata con codice PNC0000001 (Avviso D.D. 931 DEL 06.06.2022) nell'ambito della fondazione “Digital Driven Diagnostics, prognostics and therapeutics for sustainable Health care – Fondazione “D3 4 Health” (CUP B53C22005960001)

Progettualità cui si accede: • PNRR - Investimento 3.1 “Fondo per la realizzazione di un sistema integrato di infrastrutture di ricerca e innovazione” nell’ambito della Missione 4 Componente 2, in cui convergono i progetti “Terabit network for Research and Academic Big data in Italy” (CUP I53C21000370006) e “MEET – Monitoring Earth’s Evolution and Tectonics” (CUP D53C22001400005); • PNRR - Investimento 1.4 “Potenziamento strutture di ricerca e creazione di campioni nazionali di R&S su alcune Key Enabling Technologies”, nell’ambito della Missione 4 Componente 2, a cui accede il progetto “National Centre for HPC, Big Data and Quantum Computing”, relativo all’Area Tematica: “Simulazioni, calcolo e analisi dei dati ad alte prestazioni” (CUP D56G22000380006); • PNC - Iniziativa “Digital Driven Diagnostics, prognostics and therapeutics for sustainable Health care” identificata con codice PNC0000001 (Avviso D.D. 931 DEL 06.06.2022) nell'ambito della fondazione “Digital Driven Diagnostics, prognostics and therapeutics for sustainable Health care – Fondazione “D3 4 Health” (CUP B53C22005960001)

title-proc.ita: Procedura aperta per l’affidamento del servizio di gestione delle residenze universitarie sedi di Napoli e Aversa - CIG 9340889972

ita: L’appalto è costituito da un unico lotto in considerazione dell’omogeneità delle prestazioni richieste e della efficienza che ne deriva dalla gestione di un unico contratto. La suddivisione in lotti è resa, di fatto, non praticabile in quanto oltre il 90% delle prestazioni è da erogare presso le strutture a ubicate nel comune di Napoli. La gestione delle residenze universitarie prevede i seguenti servizi: Servizio di portierato reception, accoglienza e custodia, sostituito dal servizio di custodia e vigilanza in caso di chiusura della Residenza; Servizio di “Ronda e videosorveglianza da remoto”; Servizio di pulizia, sanificazione e disinfestazione; Servizio di fornitura a nolo e lavaggio biancheria; Servizio di piccola manutenzione. Da svolgersi nelle seguenti sedi: Residenza L'Orientale, in Via Brin 65c/67 Napoli (NA), per complessivi n. 144 posti alloggio; Residenza Parthenope, in Via Galileo Ferraris 273 Napoli (NA), per complessivi n. 180 posti alloggio; Residenza Aversa (al momento non attiva), in Via Castello nr. 24 Aversa (CE), per complessivi n. 46 posti alloggio; Residenza Paolella (al momento non attiva), in Via Tansillo 28 Napoli (NA) , per complessivi n. 94 posti alloggio; Residenza De Amicis (al momento non attiva), in Via Tommaso De Amicis, 111 Napoli NA, per complessivi n. 114 posti alloggio.
A.Di.S.U.R.C. Azienda per il Diritto allo Studio Universitario della Regione Campania
Romeo Gestioni S.p.A.

L’appalto ha per oggetto l’affidamento del servizio di gestione delle residenze universitarie sedi di Napoli e Aversa. Il servizio ha la durata di 48 mesi a decorrere dalla data di avvio rinnovabile per ulteriori 24 mesi. La gara è stata indetta con Decreto del Direttore Generale dell’ADiSURC n. 834/67/CRA1 del 26 luglio 2022. Si applica il D.Lgs. 18.04.2016, n. 50 e sue successive modificazioni ed integrazioni, nonché le altre norme di legge e regolamento espressamente richiamate nel capitolato o comunque applicabili ai servizi oggetto dell’appalto.

ita: PROCEDURA DI GARA APERTA PER L’AFFIDAMENTO DEL SERVIZIO DI MONITORAGGIO DI PRESSIONI AGENTI SU HABITAT D’INTERESSE COMUNITARIO NEL TERRITORIO DEI PARCHI NAZIONALI, TRAMITE SENSORISTICA AVANZATA CUP: F82H22000730006 LOTTO 1: Progettazione, raccolta ed elaborazione dati sulle pressioni agenti su habitat d’interesse Comunitario che si trovano all’interno dei Parchi Nazionali attraverso l’utilizzo di remote sensing (drone multispettrale e lidar) LOTTO 2: Progettazione, raccolta ed elaborazione dati sulle pressioni agenti su habitat d’interesse Comunitario che si trovano all’interno dei Parchi Nazionali attraverso l’utilizzo di proximal sensors quali Laser Scanner terrestri portatili PIANO NAZIONALE DI RIPRESA E RESILIENZA (PNRR) MISSIONE 2 “TRANSIZIONE ECOLOGICA E RIVOLUZIONE VERDE”, COMPONENTE 4 “TUTELA DEL TERRITORIO E DELLA RISORSA IDRICA”, LINEA DI INTERVENTO 3 “SALVAGUARDARE LA QUALITÀ DELL’ARIA E LA BIODIVERSITÀ DEL TERRITORIO ATTRAVERSO LA TUTELA DELLE AREE VERDI, DEL SUOLO E DELLE AREE MARINE”, INVESTIMENTO 3.2 “DIGITALIZZAZIONE DEI PARCHI NAZIONALI E DELLE AREE MARINE PROTETTE” Sub- investimento 3.2 a) “Conservazione della natura - monitoraggio delle pressioni e minacce su specie e habitat e cambiamento climatico” [M2C4-I3.2] • Target T2 – 2024: Sviluppo di servizi digitali in almeno il 70% dei parchi nazionali e aree marine protette.

description-proc.ita: L’Azienda utilizza i software applicativi della Dedalus Spa, per la gestione completa della cartella clinica informatizzata (Galileo), per la gestione di laboratori specialistici (Microbiologia), attività di consulenza, pagamento on line prestazioni SSN e portale referti. Considerato l’avvio del SIO Regionale previsto per fine 2024, primi del 2025, si rende necessario mantenere la manutenzione e l’assistenza degli applicativi in uso, per un periodo di 12 mesi fatto salvo recesso anticipato per l’avvio degli applicativi regionali. Si ipotizza un decremento progressivo dei servizi in relazione alle funzioni che verranno attivate dal nuovo SIO Regione Veneto.

title-proc.ita: Sistema di qualificazione degli operatori economici della GORI S.p.A.

ita: Il Sistema di Qualificazione ha lo scopo di istituire l'elenco degli operatori economici (fornitori) idonei, per specializzazione e per capacità, a concorrere alle procedure per l’affidamento di forniture, servizi e lavori occorrenti per l’espletamento delle diverse attività della GORI S.p.A., secondo le modalità previste dal d. lgs. 36/2023. I fornitori sono identificati e classificati secondo la tipologia di forniture, servizi, lavori e servizi di ingegneria e architettura in categorie di acquisto e, all'interno di ciascuna di esse, in classi di importo, così come disciplinato all'articolo 3 del Regolamento del Sistema di Qualificazione e nei relativi allegati. Le modalità di gestione del Sistema di Qualificazione, i requisiti che devono essere posseduti dagli operatori economici per poter essere qualificati e la relativa documentazione da presentare sono specificati nel Regolamento del Sistema di Qualificazione. Il sistema di qualificazione comprende anche il vendor rating ed il vendor monitoring per i fornitori qualificati per le categorie di acquisto critical e per determinate classi di importo.
GORI s.p.a.

title-proc.ita: FORNITURA DI HARDWARE PER IL POTENZIAMENTO DEL SISTEMA DI SUPERCALCOLO GALILEO 100 E RELATIVI SERVIZI CONNESSI

ita: CINECA Consorzio Interuniversitario in veste di stazione appaltante delegata da parte dell’Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale e dall’Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, intende procedere, in applicazione dell’art. 62, comma 14, d.lgs. 36/2023, all’acquisizione di un sistema che erogherà servizi di calcolo ad alte prestazioni e di virtualizzazione per le infrastrutture di ricerca e per la comunità di utenti CINECA, affiancando e complementando il sistema adacloud (https://adacloud.hpc.cineca.it/) e i sistemi HPC Tier0 e Tier1 già operativi. Progettualità cui si accede: • PNRR - Investimento 3.1 “Fondo per la realizzazione di un sistema integrato di infrastrutture di ricerca e innovazione” nell’ambito della Missione 4 Componente 2, in cui convergono i progetti “Terabit network for Research and Academic Big data in Italy” (CUP I53C21000370006) e “MEET – Monitoring Earth’s Evolution and Tectonics” (CUP D53C22001400005); • PNRR - Investimento 1.4 “Potenziamento strutture di ricerca e creazione di campioni nazionali di R&S su alcune Key Enabling Technologies”, nell’ambito della Missione 4 Componente 2, a cui accede il progetto “National Centre for HPC, Big Data and Quantum Computing”, relativo all’Area Tematica: “Simulazioni, calcolo e analisi dei dati ad alte prestazioni” (CUP D56G22000380006); • PNC - Iniziativa “Digital Driven Diagnostics, prognostics and therapeutics for sustainable Health care” identificata con codice PNC0000001 (Avviso D.D. 931 DEL 06.06.2022) nell'ambito della fondazione “Digital Driven Diagnostics, prognostics and therapeutics for sustainable Health care – Fondazione “D3 4 Health” (CUP B53C22005960001)
CINECA CONSORZIO INTERUNIVERSITARIO
E4 COMPUTER ENGINEERING S.p.A.

description-proc.ita: CINECA Consorzio Interuniversitario in veste di stazione appaltante delegata da parte dell’Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale e dall’Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, intende procedere, in applicazione dell’art. 62, comma 14, d.lgs. 36/2023, all’acquisizione di un sistema che erogherà servizi di calcolo ad alte prestazioni e di virtualizzazione per le infrastrutture di ricerca e per la comunità di utenti CINECA, affiancando e complementando il sistema adacloud (https://adacloud.hpc.cineca.it/) e i sistemi HPC Tier0 e Tier1 già operativi. Progettualità cui si accede: • PNRR - Investimento 3.1 “Fondo per la realizzazione di un sistema integrato di infrastrutture di ricerca e innovazione” nell’ambito della Missione 4 Componente 2, in cui convergono i progetti “Terabit network for Research and Academic Big data in Italy” (CUP I53C21000370006) e “MEET – Monitoring Earth’s Evolution and Tectonics” (CUP D53C22001400005); • PNRR - Investimento 1.4 “Potenziamento strutture di ricerca e creazione di campioni nazionali di R&S su alcune Key Enabling Technologies”, nell’ambito della Missione 4 Componente 2, a cui accede il progetto “National Centre for HPC, Big Data and Quantum Computing”, relativo all’Area Tematica: “Simulazioni, calcolo e analisi dei dati ad alte prestazioni” (CUP D56G22000380006); • PNC - Iniziativa “Digital Driven Diagnostics, prognostics and therapeutics for sustainable Health care” identificata con codice PNC0000001 (Avviso D.D. 931 DEL 06.06.2022) nell'ambito della fondazione “Digital Driven Diagnostics, prognostics and therapeutics for sustainable Health care – Fondazione “D3 4 Health” (CUP B53C22005960001)

Lotto 3 - Fornitura n. 2.280 fototrappole con accessori connessi necessari al loro funzionamento (n. 2280 box di sicurezza con lucchetto, n. 4.560 schede SD, n. 54.720 batterie ricaricabili AA, n. 342 caricabatterie multislot); n. 58 di videocamere remotabili; N. 2.940 cassette nido e 4.000 footprint tunnels.

Lotto 4 - Fornitura n. 3.976 registratori digitali audio per il monitoraggio di uccelli canori e relativi accessori (n. 7.952 schede di memoria SD/microSD da 32Gb, n. 31.808 batterie AA); n. 675 registratore digitali audio per il monitoraggio di chirotteri e relativi accessori (n. 1.350 schede di memoria SD/microSD da 64Gb; 5.400 batterie AA).
Lotto 5 - Fornitura n. 143 GPS portatili satellitari.

ita: PROCEDURA DI GARA APERTA PER L’AFFIDAMENTO DEL SERVIZIO DI MONITORAGGIO DI PRESSIONI AGENTI SU HABITAT D’INTERESSE COMUNITARIO NEL TERRITORIO DEI PARCHI NAZIONALI, TRAMITE SENSORISTICA AVANZATA CUP: F82H22000730006 LOTTO 1: Progettazione, raccolta ed elaborazione dati sulle pressioni agenti su habitat d’interesse Comunitario che si trovano all’interno dei Parchi Nazionali attraverso l’utilizzo di remote sensing (drone multispettrale e lidar) CIG: B1E0B077CC LOTTO 2: Progettazione, raccolta ed elaborazione dati sulle pressioni agenti su habitat d’interesse Comunitario che si trovano all’interno dei Parchi Nazionali attraverso l’utilizzo di proximal sensors quali Laser Scanner terrestri portatili CIG: B1E0B0889F PIANO NAZIONALE DI RIPRESA E RESILIENZA (PNRR) MISSIONE 2 “TRANSIZIONE ECOLOGICA E RIVOLUZIONE VERDE”, COMPONENTE 4 “TUTELA DEL TERRITORIO E DELLA RISORSA IDRICA”, LINEA DI INTERVENTO 3 “SALVAGUARDARE LA QUALITÀ DELL’ARIA E LA BIODIVERSITÀ DEL TERRITORIO ATTRAVERSO LA TUTELA DELLE AREE VERDI, DEL SUOLO E DELLE AREE MARINE”, INVESTIMENTO 3.2 “DIGITALIZZAZIONE DEI PARCHI NAZIONALI E DELLE AREE MARINE PROTETTE” Sub- investimento 3.2 a) “Conservazione della natura - monitoraggio delle pressioni e minacce su specie e habitat e cambiamento climatico” [M2C4-I3.2] • Target T2 – 2024: Sviluppo di servizi digitali in almeno il 70% dei parchi nazionali e aree marine protette.

title-proc.ita: CdC per MASE |PNRR|: PROCEDURA DI GARA APERTA IN 5 LOTTI PER L’AFFIDAMENTO DELLA FORNITURA DI “STRUMENTAZIONE PER IL MONITORAGGIO DELLA FAUNA SELVATICA DA DESTINARE AI PARCHI NAZIONALI”

ita: Lotto1 - Fornitura n. 332 telescopi ad alta qualità con custodia, cavalletto in carbonio e testa video; n. 380 binocoli ad alta qualità; n. 111 binocoli ad alta qualità con telemetro laser.
Lotto 2 - Fornitura n. 114 binocoli termici ad alta risoluzione con telemetro laser integrato.

Lotto 3 - Fornitura n. 2.280 fototrappole con accessori connessi necessari al loro funzionamento (n. 2280 box di sicurezza con lucchetto, n. 4.560 schede SD, n. 54.720 batterie ricaricabili AA, n. 342 caricabatterie multislot); n. 58 di videocamere remotabili; N. 2.940 cassette nido e 4.000 footprint tunnels.

Lotto 4 - Fornitura n. 3.976 registratori digitali audio per il monitoraggio di uccelli canori e relativi accessori (n. 7.952 schede di memoria SD/microSD da 32Gb, n. 31.808 batterie AA); n. 675 registratore digitali audio per il monitoraggio di chirotteri e relativi accessori (n. 1.350 schede di memoria SD/microSD da 64Gb; 5.400 batterie AA).
Lotto 5 - Fornitura n. 143 GPS portatili satellitari.
